## Proposal

### What is the root cause of that problem?

This is new-content work, not a code defect. The persistent bottom-right window built in #95791 is content-driven: it renders whatever `ACTIVE_PRODUCT_MARKETING_ANNOUNCEMENT` contains, and that constant is still pinned to the July 2026 announcement (admin-only, no member variant):

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L57-L66

One gap does need a small code change: the August admin CTA must branch on whether Vendors is already enabled ("more features" page vs. the direct vendors URL), but the current `getCtaRoute` contract only receives the target workspace ID, so a variant can't inspect the policy's feature state:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L36-L37

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

1. In `ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts`, replace the July announcement with a new one using a fresh `updateKey` (e.g. `productUpdateAugust2026`) so users who dismissed July see August. Fill both variants: `admin` = "Enhanced vendor mapping" with the vendor-list marketing image, `member` = "Pre-built agents for you" with the agents-list image, both with a "Try it out" CTA. New strings go under `productMarketingWindow` in `en.ts`/`es.ts` next to the existing July block:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/languages/en.ts#L10534-L10540

2. Widen `getCtaRoute` to receive the target admin `Policy` object (and the vendor-matching beta flag) instead of just the ID. The manager already resolves the full policy list, so it can pass the found policy through where it currently passes only `targetAdminPolicyID`:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/components/ProductMarketingWindow/ProductMarketingWindowManager.tsx#L67-L68

The admin variant's `getCtaRoute` then reuses the same check the More Features page uses, `hasVendorFeature`:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/libs/PolicyUtils.ts#L2438-L2442

returning `ROUTES.WORKSPACE_VENDORS.getRoute(policy.id)` when vendors are on, otherwise `ROUTES.WORKSPACE_MORE_FEATURES.getRoute(policy.id)`. The member variant's `getCtaRoute` simply returns `ROUTES.SETTINGS_AGENTS_NEW.getRoute()`. All display/dismiss/precedence logic in the manager and window component stays untouched.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

Keep `getCtaRoute(policyID)` as-is and do the vendors-enabled branch inside the manager's `completeCta`. Rejected because it leaks announcement-specific logic into the shared manager; keeping routing decisions inside the variant keeps future updates content-only.

note: Withdrawn in production against the linked proposal. Two priors, so there is only one plausible answer.

priorProposals.body:
## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.

The August 2026 product update needs a persistent bottom-right product marketing window, reusing the pattern built for the July update in issue #95791. There are two audience variants: admins should see "Enhanced vendor mapping" with a Try it out button that leads them to enable (or use) Vendors on their active admin workspace, and employees should see "Pre-built agents for you" with a Try it out button that opens the new-agent flow at `settings/agents/new`.

### What is the root cause of that problem?

This is a new feature request rather than a bug. The persistent window system built for #95791 is intentionally config-driven: exactly one announcement is active at a time, defined by `ACTIVE_PRODUCT_MARKETING_ANNOUNCEMENT` in `ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts`, and it currently still holds the July 2026 update (`productUpdateJuly2026`) with an admin-only variant:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1e9d3c3ef392d36aac215f5a93bc54f047211c59/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L52-L66

No August announcement has been authored yet, so nothing new is shown. Additionally, the announcement's CTA route builder currently only receives the target admin workspace ID, which is not enough for the August admin CTA — that CTA must branch on whether the workspace's Vendors feature is already enabled:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1e9d3c3ef392d36aac215f5a93bc54f047211c59/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L36-L37

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

Replace the active announcement in `ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts` with an August 2026 announcement using a new update key (for example `productUpdateAugust2026`). Because dismissal is tracked by comparing the update key against the `lastDismissedMarketingWindow` NVP, users who dismissed the July window will automatically see the August one — no changes to the dismissal, targeting, or visibility logic are needed:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1e9d3c3ef392d36aac215f5a93bc54f047211c59/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L68-L86

**Admin variant** — heading "Enhanced vendor mapping", body "Create vendors and custom rules for easy mapping to major accounting packages.", CTA "Try it out". The CTA should navigate to the Vendors page (`workspaces/<policyID>/vendors`, the existing `WORKSPACE_VENDORS` route) when the target workspace's Vendors feature is already on, and otherwise to the More features page (`workspaces/<policyID>/more-features`, the existing `WORKSPACE_MORE_FEATURES` route) where the admin can turn Vendors on. Whether Vendors is on is exactly what the existing `hasVendorFeature` helper answers (vendor-matching beta plus a supported accounting connection), the same check the More features page uses for its Vendors toggle:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1e9d3c3ef392d36aac215f5a93bc54f047211c59/src/libs/PolicyUtils.ts#L2438-L2443

To support that branch, extend the announcement variant's CTA route builder so it receives the resolved target admin workspace's full policy object and the vendor-matching beta state, not just the workspace ID. `ProductMarketingWindowManager` already holds the full active admin policy objects (it currently narrows them down to `targetAdminPolicyID`), and it can read the beta via the existing permissions hook, so it passes both into the route builder:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1e9d3c3ef392d36aac215f5a93bc54f047211c59/src/components/ProductMarketingWindow/ProductMarketingWindowManager.tsx#L67-L68

The existing target-workspace selection already implements "their active workspace they are an admin on" (the active policy when the user is an admin on it, otherwise their first active admin workspace), so it is kept as is.

**Member (employee) variant** — heading "Pre-built agents for you", body "Use pre-built or custom agents to code, split, and submit expenses automatically on your behalf.", CTA "Try it out" navigating to the existing `SETTINGS_AGENTS_NEW` route (`settings/agents/new`), which matches the URL requested in the issue. The member variant is already optional in the announcement type and the manager already falls back to it for users with no active admin workspace, so adding it is pure configuration:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1e9d3c3ef392d36aac215f5a93bc54f047211c59/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L40-L50

**Copy and translations** — add the August heading/body/CTA strings for both variants under the existing `productMarketingWindow` namespace in `en.ts`, remove the now-unused July keys, and generate the other locales the standard way.

**Visuals** — the window's visual field already accepts either a bundled marketing image or an existing app illustration. Once the design mocks land (vendor-list image for the admin case, agents-list image for the employee case), add them as bundled assets the same way the July promo image was added; until then an existing relevant illustration can serve as the interim visual so the window is fully functional for review.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

Building the August window as a second, parallel announcement alongside the July one was ruled out — the system is deliberately single-active with no stacking or queueing, and replacing the active announcement is the intended release mechanism. Always sending the admin CTA to the More features page (skipping the vendors-enabled branch) was also ruled out because the issue explicitly asks for the direct destination when Vendors is already on.

priorProposals.body:
## Proposal

### What is the root cause of that problem?

The persistent bottom-right product marketing window system already exists (built in #95791 and driven by the dismissed-product-training NVP, e.g. the `DismissedProductTraining` selector pattern used for other banners):

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/pages/workspace/rules/PolicyRulesPageRevamp.tsx#L75-L79

There is simply no window definition for the August update, so neither the admin "Enhanced vendor mapping" card nor the employee "Pre-built agents" card renders, and their two "Try it out" destinations are not wired.

The admin CTA is also non-trivial because its target depends on whether the admin's workspace can even reach Vendors. Vendors lives inside Rules, and Rules access for a workspace is gated by `canPolicyAccessFeature` (Collect needs the Rules revamp beta, otherwise Control only):

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/libs/PolicyUtils.ts#L1453-L1465

and the Vendors toggle itself is only exposed when `VENDOR_MATCHING` is enabled on the More features page:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/pages/workspace/WorkspaceMoreFeaturesPage/index.tsx#L61-L95

So a blind link to a fixed `{policyID}/more-features` would break for members who are not admins of that workspace or whose plan cannot access Rules.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

1. Register two new product-update window entries in the same persistent-window config used by #95791 (title/subtext/image/buttons per the deliverables), each dismissible via the existing `dismissProductTraining` flow used by `RulesGeneralTab`:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/pages/workspace/rules/tabs/RulesGeneralTab.tsx#L23-L49

2. Admin case "Try it out": resolve the workspace where the current user is an admin, then route through the existing More features route. Reuse `WORKSPACE_MORE_FEATURES.getRoute(policyID)` already used on that page:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/pages/workspace/WorkspaceMoreFeaturesPage/index.tsx#L353-L387

When Vendors is already on for that workspace, deep-link straight to the Rules Vendors screen instead of More features:

```ts
const canAccessRules = canPolicyAccessFeature(policy, CONST.POLICY.MORE_FEATURES.ARE_RULES_ENABLED, isRulesRevampEnabled);
const vendorsAlreadyOn = isVendorMatchingEnabled && canAccessRules && arePolicyRulesEnabled(policy, policyCategories, isRulesRevampEnabled);
Navigation.navigate(vendorsAlreadyOn ? ROUTES.WORKSPACE_RULES.getRoute(policyID) : ROUTES.WORKSPACE_MORE_FEATURES.getRoute(policyID));
```

This mirrors the exact enablement checks in `useControlOnlyRuleUpgradeRedirect`, so the CTA never lands a member on a page their plan cannot use:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/hooks/useControlOnlyRuleUpgradeRedirect.ts#L25-L45

3. Employee case "Try it out": navigate to the new-agent route (`/settings/agents/new`) using its `ROUTES` constant, matching the CTA behavior of the existing `AgentPromotionalBanner` in `RulesGeneralTab`.

This adds the missing window definitions and gives each CTA a destination that respects admin membership and Rules/Vendors availability.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

Always link the admin CTA to a fixed `more-features` URL and let `AccessOrNotFoundWrapper` redirect, but that flashes an inaccessible page for non-admins or non-Rules plans, so resolving the correct workspace and gate up front is cleaner.

**Reminder:** Please use plain English, be brief and avoid jargon. Feel free to use images, charts or pseudo-code if necessary. Do not post large multi-line diffs or write walls of text. Do not create PRs unless you have been hired for this job.

## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.

On the Spend (Search) page the date filter and the date column are both just labelled "Date", which is ambiguous next to Submitted/Approved/Posted/Exported. The filter option should read **"Created date"** and the column header **"Created"**, for every search Type.

### What is the root cause of that problem?

There is no Search-scoped label for this field. Both places render the generic key `common.date`, and they read it through **three independent sources**, so no single edit can produce the two different strings the issue asks for.

1. The string is `common.date: 'Date'` — [en.ts#L168](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/languages/en.ts#L168). It has 23 references in 16 files (expense edit, personal details, travel, wallet, `MoneyRequestView`), so its value is not ours to change.
2. **Source A — filter label:** `FILTER_VIEW_MAP[SYNTAX_FILTER_KEYS.DATE].labelKey = 'common.date'` — [SearchUIUtils.ts#L5527-L5530](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L5527-L5530).
3. **Source B — column label:** `getSearchColumnTranslationKey()` maps `TABLE_COLUMNS.DATE` → `'common.date'` — [SearchUIUtils.ts#L4508-L4513](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L4508-L4513).
4. **Source C — the header rows do not use B.** `SearchTableHeader` hardcodes `translationKey: 'common.date'` a third time, once per data type, rendered by [SortableTableHeader.tsx#L92](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/components/Search/SortableTableHeader.tsx#L92).

Structural cause: **one overloaded generic key is doing three jobs** — generic "Date", the Search filter label, the Search column label — and the issue requires those to diverge.

Every affected path:

*Source A → "Created date":*
- Filters list row — [FilterList.tsx#L54](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/components/Search/FilterComponents/AdvancedFilters/FilterList.tsx#L54)
- Filter page title — [SearchAdvancedFiltersContentBase.tsx#L61](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/pages/Search/SearchAdvancedFiltersContentPage/SearchAdvancedFiltersContentBase.tsx#L61)
- Applied-filter pill — [useSearchFiltersBar.tsx#L62](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/components/Search/SearchPageHeader/useSearchFiltersBar.tsx#L62)
- Saved-search summary — [SearchUIUtils.ts#L5903-L5905](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L5903-L5905)

*Sources B + C → "Created":*
- Expense headers — [SearchTableHeader.tsx#L44-L48](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx#L44-L48); Task — [#L209-L212](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx#L209-L212); Expense-report — [#L252-L255](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx#L252-L255)
- Column picker — [ColumnsSettingsList.tsx#L123](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/components/ColumnsSettingsList.tsx#L123)
- Sort-by dropdown — [getSortByOptions](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L5131-L5138) + [DisplayPopup.tsx#L86](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/components/Search/FilterDropdowns/DisplayPopup.tsx#L86)
- Saved-search sort/columns — [SearchSavePage.tsx#L131](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/pages/Search/SearchSavePage.tsx#L131), [#L145](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/pages/Search/SearchSavePage.tsx#L145)
- CSV export header — [useSearchBulkActions.ts#L825](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/hooks/useSearchBulkActions.ts#L825)

**Narrow layout is covered by the same change:** `SearchTableHeader` returns nothing below wide ([#L606-L608](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx#L606-L608)), so on small/medium screens the label only appears via the sort dropdown and column picker — both of which go through `getSearchColumnTranslationKey`.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

1. Add two Search-scoped keys beside the existing siblings `posted`/`exported`/`submitted` in [en.ts#L9174-L9180](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/languages/en.ts#L9174-L9180):

```ts
// src/languages/en.ts -> search.filters
createdDate: 'Created date',
created: 'Created',
```

2. Mirror both keys into the other 10 locale files (`es`, `fr`, `de`, `it`, `nl`, `pl`, `pt-BR`, `ja`, `zh-hans`, `el`). Required, not optional: each is typed `TranslationDeepObject<typeof en>` ([es.ts#L19](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/languages/es.ts#L19)), a total mapping, so omitting them fails `tsc`.
3. Point the filter label at `'search.filters.createdDate'` — [SearchUIUtils.ts#L5528](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L5528).
4. Point the column label at `'search.filters.created'` in `getSearchColumnTranslationKey` ([#L4513](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L4513)) **and** in all three `SearchTableHeader` arrays (L46, L211, L254).

Regression safety: `common.date` keeps the value `'Date'`, so all 23 non-Search usages (expense date edit, travel, wallet, `MoneyRequestView`) and every sibling filter label are untouched.

**Why the obvious one-line fix does not work.** Editing `common.date` → `'Created date'` renames "Date" in 16 unrelated files, and still cannot satisfy the issue because the filter and column need *two different* strings from one key. Repointing only `getSearchColumnTranslationKey` also fails: `SearchTableHeader` never calls it — it holds its own `translationKey: 'common.date'` literals — so the column picker and sort menu would say "Created" while the table header still said "Date". Sources B and C must move together.

**Do not touch the query key.** `[TABLE_COLUMNS.DATE]: 'date'` in [CONST/index.ts#L7542](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/CONST/index.ts#L7542) is the wire value for `date:` search syntax and the `sortBy` sent to the backend. This is display copy only; renaming that constant would break saved searches and the API.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

1. **Change `common.date` in place.** Rejected — 23 call sites in 16 files, and it cannot yield two distinct strings.
2. **One key (`created`) reused for both.** Rejected — the issue asks for "Created date" in filters and "Created" in the header.
3. **Make `SearchTableHeader` derive labels from `getSearchColumnTranslationKey` so source C disappears.** A real cleanup that removes the duplicate label source for good, but it touches ~30 header entries; happy to do it here or as a follow-up.
4. Bulk-edit's date field ([SearchEditMultiplePage.tsx#L280](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/pages/Search/SearchEditMultiple/SearchEditMultiplePage.tsx#L280)) stays "Date" — it edits the value, it is not a filter or column. Happy to align it if you prefer.

note: Withdrawn in production. Both proposals add Search-scoped translation keys and repoint the same filter map and column header at them.

priorProposals.body:
## Proposal

### What is the root cause of that problem?

This is a copy/labeling feature, so there's no defect — just two on-screen strings that need dedicated translation keys. Both the **filter option** and the **results column header** currently resolve to the shared `common.date` key (`'Date'`), so today they read "Date" and there's no separate string to change without hitting the ~dozen unrelated places that reuse `common.date` (IOU date step, DistanceEReceipt, Travel trip details, SearchEditMultiple, etc.).

Three distinct surfaces render that label, all pointing at `common.date`:

1. **Filter option label** ("Date" → want "Created date"). The date filter's label comes from `FILTER_VIEW_MAP[DATE].labelKey`, which is `'common.date'`: [`SearchUIUtils.ts#L5391-L5394`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/68f0046bf248e1dc43b1477f1eb4a4a3ef2812c1/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L5391-L5394). That single `labelKey` feeds the filter button/chip label, the popup title, and the applied-filter chip — e.g. `label = translate(FILTER_VIEW_MAP[baseFilterKey].labelKey)` at [`useSearchFiltersBar.tsx#L62`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/68f0046bf248e1dc43b1477f1eb4a4a3ef2812c1/src/components/Search/SearchPageHeader/useSearchFiltersBar.tsx#L62). It's type-agnostic, which is why one change covers all Types.

2. **Results table column header** ("Date" → want "Created"). The header text is the `translationKey` on the DATE column in the three header builders in `SearchTableHeader.tsx`, each hard-coded to `'common.date'`:
   - `getExpenseHeaders` (Expense / Invoice / Trip) — [`#L46`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/68f0046bf248e1dc43b1477f1eb4a4a3ef2812c1/src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx#L46)
   - `taskHeaders` (Task) — [`#L206`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/68f0046bf248e1dc43b1477f1eb4a4a3ef2812c1/src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx#L206)
   - `getExpenseReportHeaders` (Expense report) — [`#L249`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/68f0046bf248e1dc43b1477f1eb4a4a3ef2812c1/src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx#L249)

   Note its siblings already use dedicated keys (`search.filters.posted`, `.approved`, `.exported`) — DATE is the odd one still on `common.date`.

3. **Adjacent surfaces that name the same column** — the sort-by dropdown, the show/hide-columns settings list, and the Save-search summary all label the DATE column via `getSearchColumnTranslationKey`, which also returns `'common.date'`: [`SearchUIUtils.ts#L4437-L4438`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/68f0046bf248e1dc43b1477f1eb4a4a3ef2812c1/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L4437-L4438). If we only touch #2, the header says "Created" while the sort dropdown and column toggle still say "Date" — the exact "which date is this?" confusion the issue is trying to kill.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

Layer: **config/translation copy only.** No logic changes.

1. Add two dedicated keys next to the existing sibling column labels under `search.filters` in every `src/languages/*.ts` (anchor: [`en.ts#L9174`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/68f0046bf248e1dc43b1477f1eb4a4a3ef2812c1/src/languages/en.ts#L9174), where `posted`/`approved`/`exported` already live):
   - `createdDate: 'Created date'` — filter option label
   - `created: 'Created'` — column header

   (Neither key exists today.) Provide translated values for the non-English locales too.

2. Point the filter label at the new key: in `FILTER_VIEW_MAP[DATE]`, change `labelKey` from `'common.date'` to `'search.filters.createdDate'` ([`SearchUIUtils.ts#L5392`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/68f0046bf248e1dc43b1477f1eb4a4a3ef2812c1/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L5391-L5394)).

3. Point the column header at the new key: change `translationKey: 'common.date'` → `'search.filters.created'` in all three builders ([`#L46`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/68f0046bf248e1dc43b1477f1eb4a4a3ef2812c1/src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx#L46), [`#L206`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/68f0046bf248e1dc43b1477f1eb4a4a3ef2812c1/src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx#L206), [`#L249`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/68f0046bf248e1dc43b1477f1eb4a4a3ef2812c1/src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx#L249)).

4. For consistency, align `getSearchColumnTranslationKey`'s DATE case to return `'search.filters.created'` instead of `'common.date'` ([`SearchUIUtils.ts#L4438`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/68f0046bf248e1dc43b1477f1eb4a4a3ef2812c1/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L4437-L4438)), so the sort-by dropdown, columns-settings list, and Save-search summary say "Created" and match the header. This is slightly beyond the literal ask, so I'd get Design to confirm they want those three surfaces renamed too — but leaving them as "Date" reintroduces the ambiguity the issue is about.

I'd keep `common.date` untouched — the ~dozen unrelated consumers must stay "Date".

Edge cases this actually touches: the DATE column means the created/transaction date across every Type (`taskColumnNamesToSortingProperty` and `expenseReportColumnNamesToSortingProperty` already sort it by `created`), so "Created" is accurate everywhere. Grouped-transaction headers have no DATE column, so nothing to change there.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

## Proposal

### What is the root cause of that problem?

This is the narrow-layout **pre-insert/reveal** fast path for expense submit, and the Self DM gets dropped from the back stack when the destination workspace chat is pre-mounted under the confirmation RHP.

Walking the chain (all narrow/iOS):

1. You're on Self DM, so the topmost fullscreen under the confirmation RHP is `REPORTS_SPLIT_NAVIGATOR` with routes `[Sidebar, SelfDM]`. On the confirmation screen, `getSubmitExpensePreMountDestinationRoute` returns the workspace report route to pre-mount, because we're inside the Reports split navigator (`isReportTopmostSplitNavigator()`) with a *different* report focused — [`getSubmitExpensePreMountDestinationRoute.ts#L61-L92`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/pages/iou/request/step/confirmation/getSubmitExpensePreMountDestinationRoute.ts#L61-L92).

2. `usePreMountDestination` schedules the pre-insert after the RHP open transition — [`usePreMountDestination/index.ts#L125-L139`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/hooks/usePreMountDestination/index.ts#L125-L139) → `runPreInsert` → [`Navigation.ts#L1116-L1158`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/libs/Navigation/Navigation.ts#L1116-L1158), which dispatches `REPLACE_FULLSCREEN_UNDER_RHP`.

3. Because a report's outermost fullscreen is the `TAB_NAVIGATOR` wrapper, the action takes the **tab-switch** branch and rebuilds the Reports split via `getTabStateWithFocusedTarget` → `getTargetTabRoute` — [`GetStateForActionHandlers.ts#L432-L462`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/createRootStackNavigator/GetStateForActionHandlers.ts#L432-L462).

4. **The actual bug:** `getTargetTabRoute` only ever prepends the **first** existing route (`existingFirstRoute` = the sidebar) as the back target, and throws away everything else in the existing nested stack — [`GetStateForActionHandlers.ts#L218-L237`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/createRootStackNavigator/GetStateForActionHandlers.ts#L218-L237). So `[Sidebar, SelfDM]` is rebuilt as `[Sidebar, WorkspaceReport]`. **Self DM is gone.**

5. Tapping *Create expense* selects `REPORT_PRE_INSERT`; since the route is already pre-inserted, reveal just dismisses the RHP — [`SubmitExpenseOrchestrator.tsx#L229-L243`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/pages/iou/request/step/confirmation/SubmitExpenseOrchestrator.tsx#L229-L243) → exposes `TAB_NAVIGATOR[REPORTS_SPLIT[Sidebar, WorkspaceReport]]`. Back on the workspace chat pops to Sidebar = **Inbox**. 🐛

Why iOS/narrow only: pre-insert is narrow-only (`getSubmitExpensePreMountDestinationRoute` returns `undefined` on wide, [line 44](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/pages/iou/request/step/confirmation/getSubmitExpensePreMountDestinationRoute.ts#L44)), and on wide there is no report back button, so the dropped Self DM history isn't user-visible.

The tell that this is the pre-insert path and not a plain `navigate`: if you tap *Create expense* fast enough that the pre-insert idle task hasn't fired, the handler falls to `DISMISS_MODAL` → `dismissNarrowWithReport` → `dismissModalWithReport`, whose `navigate()` **pushes** the workspace report onto `[Sidebar, SelfDM]` → `[Sidebar, SelfDM, WorkspaceReport]`, and back correctly returns to Self DM ([`submitDismissStrategies.ts#L34-L50`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/pages/iou/request/step/confirmation/submitDismissStrategies.ts#L34-L50), [`Navigation.ts#L904-L941`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/libs/Navigation/Navigation.ts#L904-L941)). The pre-insert path and the push path diverge — only the pre-insert path drops the report.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

Fix layer: **navigation state** — `getTargetTabRoute` in `GetStateForActionHandlers.ts`.

When the tab being replaced is the **same** tab as the incoming target (both `REPORTS_SPLIT_NAVIGATOR`) and the existing nested stack already has a focused report that differs from the incoming report, preserve the existing nested routes and append the destination as the new top, instead of collapsing to `[existingFirstRoute, destination]`. Concretely, in the prepend block at [lines 232-237](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/createRootStackNavigator/GetStateForActionHandlers.ts#L232-L237), for the same-tab report-to-report case use the full existing `[Sidebar, SelfDM]` as the base and push `WorkspaceReport` → `[Sidebar, SelfDM, WorkspaceReport]`. That makes the reveal path produce the same stack the push path already produces, so back returns to Self DM.

Keep the current behavior for the cross-tab / global-create reveals (Search→report, Home→report), where collapsing to the sidebar back-target is intended — the change should be scoped to "same focused tab, different report already open."

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

- **Gate the report pre-insert instead of fixing the tab rebuild.** In `getSubmitExpensePreMountDestinationRoute`, skip pre-insert when `isReportTopmostSplitNavigator()` is true and the topmost report differs from `destinationReportID`, letting the flow fall back to `dismissModalWithReport`'s push (which is already correct). Rejected as the primary fix: it throws away the pre-mount perf win for the very common "submit an expense from inside a chat" flow. Worth keeping as the lower-risk option if touching shared `getTargetTabRoute` behavior is considered too broad.

- **Rejecting the "`navigate` mutates params" hypothesis.** One reading is that `dismissModalWithReport`'s `navigate(workspaceRoute)` updates the existing `SCREENS.REPORT` entry's params instead of pushing, erasing Self DM. Falsifiable and false here on two counts: (1) on the default flow the pre-insert path (`REPORT_PRE_INSERT`) fires and `dismissModalWithReport` is never called; (2) even when it is called, Expensify's report navigation **pushes** a distinct report screen (that's how the report back-stack is built), yielding `[Sidebar, SelfDM, WorkspaceReport]` — which does *not* reproduce the bug. That path is the correct one, not the broken one.

note: Withdrawn in production, on a navigation fix rather than a copy change.

1. The string is `common.date: 'Date'` — [en.ts#L168](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/languages/en.ts#L168). It has 23 references in 16 files (expense edit, personal details, travel, wallet, `MoneyRequestView`), so its value is not ours to change.
2. **Source A — filter label:** `FILTER_VIEW_MAP[SYNTAX_FILTER_KEYS.DATE].labelKey = 'common.date'` — [SearchUIUtils.ts#L5527-L5530](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L5527-L5530).
3. **Source B — column label:** `getSearchColumnTranslationKey()` maps `TABLE_COLUMNS.DATE` → `'common.date'` — [SearchUIUtils.ts#L4508-L4513](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L4508-L4513).
4. **Source C — the header rows do not use B.** `SearchTableHeader` hardcodes `translationKey: 'common.date'` a third time, once per data type, rendered by [SortableTableHeader.tsx#L92](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/components/Search/SortableTableHeader.tsx#L92).

Structural cause: **one overloaded generic key is doing three jobs** — generic "Date", the Search filter label, the Search column label — and the issue requires those to diverge.

Every affected path:

*Source A → "Created date":*
- Filters list row — [FilterList.tsx#L54](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/components/Search/FilterComponents/AdvancedFilters/FilterList.tsx#L54)
- Filter page title — [SearchAdvancedFiltersContentBase.tsx#L61](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/pages/Search/SearchAdvancedFiltersContentPage/SearchAdvancedFiltersContentBase.tsx#L61)
- Applied-filter pill — [useSearchFiltersBar.tsx#L62](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/components/Search/SearchPageHeader/useSearchFiltersBar.tsx#L62)
- Saved-search summary — [SearchUIUtils.ts#L5903-L5905](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L5903-L5905)

*Sources B + C → "Created":*
- Expense headers — [SearchTableHeader.tsx#L44-L48](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx#L44-L48); Task — [#L209-L212](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx#L209-L212); Expense-report — [#L252-L255](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx#L252-L255)
- Column picker — [ColumnsSettingsList.tsx#L123](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/components/ColumnsSettingsList.tsx#L123)
- Sort-by dropdown — [getSortByOptions](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L5131-L5138) + [DisplayPopup.tsx#L86](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/components/Search/FilterDropdowns/DisplayPopup.tsx#L86)
- Saved-search sort/columns — [SearchSavePage.tsx#L131](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/pages/Search/SearchSavePage.tsx#L131), [#L145](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/pages/Search/SearchSavePage.tsx#L145)
- CSV export header — [useSearchBulkActions.ts#L825](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/hooks/useSearchBulkActions.ts#L825)

**Narrow layout is covered by the same change:** `SearchTableHeader` returns nothing below wide ([#L606-L608](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx#L606-L608)), so on small/medium screens the label only appears via the sort dropdown and column picker — both of which go through `getSearchColumnTranslationKey`.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

1. Add two Search-scoped keys beside the existing siblings `posted`/`exported`/`submitted` in [en.ts#L9174-L9180](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/languages/en.ts#L9174-L9180):

```ts
// src/languages/en.ts -> search.filters
createdDate: 'Created date',
created: 'Created',
```

2. Mirror both keys into the other 10 locale files (`es`, `fr`, `de`, `it`, `nl`, `pl`, `pt-BR`, `ja`, `zh-hans`, `el`). Required, not optional: each is typed `TranslationDeepObject<typeof en>` ([es.ts#L19](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/languages/es.ts#L19)), a total mapping, so omitting them fails `tsc`.
3. Point the filter label at `'search.filters.createdDate'` — [SearchUIUtils.ts#L5528](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L5528).
4. Point the column label at `'search.filters.created'` in `getSearchColumnTranslationKey` ([#L4513](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L4513)) **and** in all three `SearchTableHeader` arrays (L46, L211, L254).

Regression safety: `common.date` keeps the value `'Date'`, so all 23 non-Search usages (expense date edit, travel, wallet, `MoneyRequestView`) and every sibling filter label are untouched.

**Why the obvious one-line fix does not work.** Editing `common.date` → `'Created date'` renames "Date" in 16 unrelated files, and still cannot satisfy the issue because the filter and column need *two different* strings from one key. Repointing only `getSearchColumnTranslationKey` also fails: `SearchTableHeader` never calls it — it holds its own `translationKey: 'common.date'` literals — so the column picker and sort menu would say "Created" while the table header still said "Date". Sources B and C must move together.

**Do not touch the query key.** `[TABLE_COLUMNS.DATE]: 'date'` in [CONST/index.ts#L7542](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/CONST/index.ts#L7542) is the wire value for `date:` search syntax and the `sortBy` sent to the backend. This is display copy only; renaming that constant would break saved searches and the API.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

1. **Change `common.date` in place.** Rejected — 23 call sites in 16 files, and it cannot yield two distinct strings.
2. **One key (`created`) reused for both.** Rejected — the issue asks for "Created date" in filters and "Created" in the header.
3. **Make `SearchTableHeader` derive labels from `getSearchColumnTranslationKey` so source C disappears.** A real cleanup that removes the duplicate label source for good, but it touches ~30 header entries; happy to do it here or as a follow-up.
4. Bulk-edit's date field ([SearchEditMultiplePage.tsx#L280](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/pages/Search/SearchEditMultiple/SearchEditMultiplePage.tsx#L280)) stays "Date" — it edits the value, it is not a filter or column. Happy to align it if you prefer.

## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.

On the Spend/Search page, the date filter is labeled `Date` in the advanced filters list and the results table column is also labeled `Date`. These labels are ambiguous, so users pick the wrong date filter and think the data is wrong. We want the filter option to read `Created date` and the table column header to read `Created`, for every filter Type.

### What is the root cause of that problem?

Both the filter option label and the column header point at the shared `common.date` translation, which resolves to `Date`. There is no dedicated string that names this filter/column as the _created_ date.

The advanced‑filters list gets its label from `FILTER_VIEW_MAP` for the `DATE` key:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/87bafcdf14000c23e9c09fa7cf27ca7556b9d45b/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L5527-L5530

```ts
[CONST.SEARCH.SYNTAX_FILTER_KEYS.DATE]: {
    labelKey: 'common.date',
    icon: 'CalendarSolid',
},
```

`FilterList` renders that `labelKey`, and the filter subpage header reuses the same `FILTER_VIEW_MAP[...].labelKey`, so both surfaces show `Date`.

The results table column header maps the `DATE` column to `common.date` in all three header sets (expenses, tasks, expense reports):

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/87bafcdf14000c23e9c09fa7cf27ca7556b9d45b/src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx#L44-L48

```ts
{
    columnName: CONST.SEARCH.TABLE_COLUMNS.DATE,
    translationKey: 'common.date',
    canEdit: true,
},
```

`common.date` is used in ~20+ unrelated places (IOU date field, e‑receipts, modified‑expense messages, travel/wallet, etc.), so it can't simply be renamed:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/87bafcdf14000c23e9c09fa7cf27ca7556b9d45b/src/languages/en.ts#L168

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

Add two dedicated Search translation keys and point the two Search surfaces at them, leaving `common.date` untouched.

1. Add the keys under `search.filters` in `src/languages/en.ts` (and their Spanish equivalents in `src/languages/es.ts`):

```ts
// en.ts – inside search.filters
createdDate: 'Created date',
created: 'Created',
```

```ts
// es.ts – inside search.filters
createdDate: 'Fecha de creación',
created: 'Creado',
```

2. Use `search.filters.createdDate` for the filter option label in `FILTER_VIEW_MAP` (`src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts`). This renames both the filter row in the list and the filter subpage header, since both read this `labelKey`:

```ts
[CONST.SEARCH.SYNTAX_FILTER_KEYS.DATE]: {
    labelKey: 'search.filters.createdDate',
    icon: 'CalendarSolid',
},
```

3. Use `search.filters.created` for the `DATE` column header in `src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx`, in all three header sets — `getExpenseHeaders` (L44‑L48), `taskHeaders` (~L210), and `getExpenseReportHeaders` (~L253):

```ts
{
    columnName: CONST.SEARCH.TABLE_COLUMNS.DATE,
    translationKey: 'search.filters.created',
    canEdit: true, // keep the existing flags per header set
},
```

Because `FILTER_VIEW_MAP` and `SearchTableHeader` are shared across all data types, this covers every filter Type (Expenses, Reports, Chats/Tasks) in one place. No sorting/query logic changes — only the display label.

### What specific scenarios should we cover in automated tests to prevent this from happening again?

- Render the advanced filters `FilterList` and assert the date filter row shows `Created date` (and the date filter subpage header shows `Created date`).
- Render `SearchTableHeader` for expense, expense‑report and task data types and assert the date column header shows `Created`.
- Assert an unrelated `common.date` consumer (e.g. the IOU date field / MoneyRequestView) still shows `Date`, guarding against a shared‑key regression.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

- Renaming `common.date` directly to `Created`/`Created date`: rejected because that key is reused in ~20+ non‑Search contexts (IOU date, e‑receipts, modified‑expense messages, travel, wallet), which would mislabel all of them.
- A single shared new key for both surfaces: rejected because the two strings differ (`Created date` for the filter vs. `Created` for the column), so two keys are needed.

priorProposals.body:
# Proposal

## Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.
In Search (Reports/Expenses/Tasks), the date filter option is labeled just `Date`, and the corresponding results-table column header is also just `Date`. This is ambiguous because "Date" could mean the transaction date, submitted date, etc. Users pick this filter/column expecting it to reflect the expense's own date, see different numbers than expected, and think the data is wrong — when really they've just filtered/sorted by the wrong date field. The ask is to rename the filter option to `Created date` and the column header to `Created`, across all Search data types.

## What is the root cause of that problem?
Both surfaces render the exact same generic, app-wide translation string `common.date` ("Date") instead of a Search-specific, unambiguous label — and that string is shared with many unrelated screens, so it can't simply be reworded in place.

**Filter option label.** The "Date" entry a user picks from the filter-type list, the resulting filter chip, and the RHP page title shown when configuring it are all driven by one shared map entry:
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/4ec44bb9c9cb9445f0836d0220a01d8d252cec84/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L5527-L5530
`FILTER_VIEW_MAP[CONST.SEARCH.SYNTAX_FILTER_KEYS.DATE].labelKey` is `'common.date'`. This single `labelKey` is read by the filter-type list item (`FilterItem` in `FilterList.tsx`), the applied-filter chip builder in `SearchUIUtils.ts` (`mapFiltersFormToLabelValueList`), the filter bar chip in `useSearchFiltersBar.tsx`, and the RHP header title in `SearchAdvancedFiltersContentBase.tsx` — so every "Date" instance under Filters traces back to this one key.
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/4ec44bb9c9cb9445f0836d0220a01d8d252cec84/src/components/Search/FilterComponents/AdvancedFilters/FilterList.tsx#L54
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/4ec44bb9c9cb9445f0836d0220a01d8d252cec84/src/pages/Search/SearchAdvancedFiltersContentPage/SearchAdvancedFiltersContentBase.tsx#L61

**Column header.** The `Date` column header text comes from two places that must stay in sync: three separate `SearchColumnConfig` entries in `SearchTableHeader.tsx` (one per data type — Expense, Task, Expense Report), and a switch statement, `getSearchColumnTranslationKey()`, used everywhere else a column's display name is needed (sort-by dropdown, "Edit columns" list, save-search summary, CSV export headers).
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/4ec44bb9c9cb9445f0836d0220a01d8d252cec84/src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx#L44-L48
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/4ec44bb9c9cb9445f0836d0220a01d8d252cec84/src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx#L209-L212
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/4ec44bb9c9cb9445f0836d0220a01d8d252cec84/src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx#L252-L255
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/4ec44bb9c9cb9445f0836d0220a01d8d252cec84/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L4508-L4513
All five of these resolve to `translationKey: 'common.date'` / `'common.date'`.

**Why the string can't just be reworded.** `common.date` (defined here) is a generic, app-wide label reused far outside Search — for the expense's own transaction-date field, personal-detail date-of-birth-adjacent fields, CSV import column mapping, travel trip dates, etc.
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/4ec44bb9c9cb9445f0836d0220a01d8d252cec84/src/languages/en.ts#L168
For example it's the label used in the actual expense date picker (`IOURequestStepDate.tsx`), the money-request confirmation `DateField.tsx`, and `MoneyRequestView.tsx`. Renaming `common.date` itself would correctly fix Search but would incorrectly relabel all of those unrelated date fields to "Created date"/"Created" too. That's the actual root cause: Search is piggy-backing on a shared, non-Search-specific string instead of owning its own label, which is also why the string reads ambiguously in the first place — it was never written to describe "the report/transaction's created date" specifically. (This is corroborated by `SearchUIUtils.ts`, where the same `TABLE_COLUMNS.DATE` key is explicitly mapped to the underlying `created` sort field for expense reports and tasks — the data really is "created date", the label just never said so.)

## What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?
Add two new Search-scoped translation strings, following the exact existing pattern already used for sibling filter/column labels in the same object (`search.filters.approved`, `search.filters.submitted`, `search.filters.posted`, etc., which already double as both filter label and column header for their respective columns) — then point the Date-specific call sites at the new keys instead of the shared `common.date`. This keeps `common.date` untouched for its many unrelated usages, and requires no new files, hooks, or abstractions.

**1. Add the new strings**, right after the existing `filters.date` presets object:
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/4ec44bb9c9cb9445f0836d0220a01d8d252cec84/src/languages/en.ts#L9122-L9138
```ts
createdDate: 'Created date',
created: 'Created',
```
And the matching Spanish entries in the equivalent spot in `es.ts` (required — `es.ts` is typed as `TranslationDeepObject<typeof en>`, so it won't compile without them):
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/4ec44bb9c9cb9445f0836d0220a01d8d252cec84/src/languages/es.ts#L8889-L8901
```ts
createdDate: 'Fecha de creación',
created: 'Creación',
```

**2. Point the filter label at the new key** (used for the filter-type list item, filter chip, and RHP page title):
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/4ec44bb9c9cb9445f0836d0220a01d8d252cec84/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L5527-L5530
```ts
[CONST.SEARCH.SYNTAX_FILTER_KEYS.DATE]: {
    labelKey: 'search.filters.createdDate',
    icon: 'CalendarSolid',
},
```

**3. Point the column header at the new key**, in all three `SearchTableHeader.tsx` configs and in `getSearchColumnTranslationKey()`:
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/4ec44bb9c9cb9445f0836d0220a01d8d252cec84/src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx#L44-L48
```ts
translationKey: 'search.filters.created',
```
(same one-line change at L211 in `taskHeaders` and L254 in `getExpenseReportHeaders`)
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/4ec44bb9c9cb9445f0836d0220a01d8d252cec84/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L4508-L4513
```ts
case CONST.SEARCH.TABLE_COLUMNS.DATE:
    return 'search.filters.created';
```

Because `getSearchColumnTranslationKey()` and `FILTER_VIEW_MAP` are the single sources every other surface reads from, this automatically and correctly propagates to: the sort-by dropdown (`SearchUIUtils.ts` `getSortableColumns`), the "Edit columns" list (`ColumnsSettingsList.tsx`), the Display popup's "Sort by" text (`DisplayPopup.tsx`), the applied-filters/sort summary on Save Search (`SearchSavePage.tsx`), and CSV export column headers (`useSearchBulkActions.ts`) — no per-call-site changes needed there.

**Edge cases handled:**
- All three data-type column configs (Expense, Expense Report, Task) are updated identically, so the header reads "Created" consistently regardless of which Search type/tab is active — this matches the issue's "apply to all filter Types" requirement.
- `common.date` itself is left unchanged, so unrelated screens that reuse it (expense date picker, money request confirmation date field, personal details, CSV import mapping, travel trip details) keep showing "Date" with no regression.
- The underlying filter/sort/column identifiers (`CONST.SEARCH.SYNTAX_FILTER_KEYS.DATE = 'date'`, `CONST.SEARCH.TABLE_COLUMNS.DATE = 'date'`) are untouched — only the display strings change. Saved searches, shareable search URLs, and the `date:` search-query syntax keep working exactly as before; this is a pure label change with no data or query-parsing impact.
- This is a static string swap with no new data fetching, so offline, loading, and empty states are unaffected.
- No platform-specific code paths exist for these maps, so web, iOS, and Android all pick up the change identically; RTL is handled the same way as every other existing filter/column label (plain translated text, no special-casing needed).

## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.

On the Spend page the date filter and the date column are both labelled just "Date", which is ambiguous next to Submitted / Approved / Posted / Exported / Withdrawn. We want the filter to read "Created date" and the column header to read "Created", for every search type.

### What is the root cause of that problem?

This is a naming task rather than a defect, so the work is in finding every place the label is produced. There are two independent sources of truth, and they are not the same one.

**Filter label.** Every filter surface reads `FILTER_VIEW_MAP`, where the date entry points at `common.date`:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7242015486fbde102ab7a6b470ce4e89efae433e/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L5527-L5530

That single entry feeds the filter list row, the filter chips bar, the filter detail page title and the applied-filters summary, for example:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7242015486fbde102ab7a6b470ce4e89efae433e/src/components/Search/FilterComponents/AdvancedFilters/FilterList.tsx#L54

**Column label.** This one is duplicated. The rendered table header comes from the column config lists in `SearchTableHeader.tsx`, and there are three of them, one per group of search types, all pointing at `common.date`:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7242015486fbde102ab7a6b470ce4e89efae433e/src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx#L44-L48

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7242015486fbde102ab7a6b470ce4e89efae433e/src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx#L209-L212

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7242015486fbde102ab7a6b470ce4e89efae433e/src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx#L252-L255

Separately, `getSearchColumnTranslationKey` returns the same key for the same column:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7242015486fbde102ab7a6b470ce4e89efae433e/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L4512-L4513

and that function is what names the column in the "Edit columns" picker, the Sort by menu and the saved-search summary:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7242015486fbde102ab7a6b470ce4e89efae433e/src/components/ColumnsSettingsList.tsx#L123

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7242015486fbde102ab7a6b470ce4e89efae433e/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L5135

So a change to `SearchTableHeader.tsx` alone renames the header but leaves the picker and the sort menu still offering "Date" for that same column.

Two further points that decide whether the result actually looks right:

1. `common.date` cannot be edited in place. It is shared with the expense date field, the confirmation list, date of birth in private personal details, travel trip details and the CSV import mapper, none of which are "created" dates. The rename needs its own key.

2. The Date column has a fixed narrow width of 62px:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7242015486fbde102ab7a6b470ce4e89efae433e/src/styles/utils/index.ts#L1987-L1990

62px fits "Date" plus the sort caret, but not "Created" plus the sort caret. With only the label changed, the header renders truncated as "Creat…". The codebase already has this exact problem solved for a longer header, First approved pins a fixed 102px with a comment explaining that the header, not the date, drives the width:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7242015486fbde102ab7a6b470ce4e89efae433e/src/styles/utils/index.ts#L1977-L1980

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

**1. Add two keys** next to the sibling date-filter labels in `search.filters` (which already holds `submitted`, `approved`, `exported`, `posted`, `withdrawn`), in all 11 language files:

```
created: 'Created',
createdDate: 'Created date',
```

**2. Point the filter label at the new key.** One edit covers the filter list, the chips bar, the filter page title and the applied-filters summary, because they all read `FILTER_VIEW_MAP`:

```diff
     [CONST.SEARCH.SYNTAX_FILTER_KEYS.DATE]: {
-        labelKey: 'common.date',
+        labelKey: 'search.filters.createdDate',
         icon: 'CalendarSolid',
     },
```

**3. Point the column label at the new key in both sources of truth**, so the header, the column picker and the sort menu stay consistent: the three `translationKey: 'common.date'` entries in `SearchTableHeader.tsx`, and the `TABLE_COLUMNS.DATE` case in `getSearchColumnTranslationKey`:

```diff
         case CONST.SEARCH.TABLE_COLUMNS.DATE:
-            return 'common.date';
+            return 'search.filters.created';
```

Using the three header lists is what satisfies "this would apply to all filter Types": the first covers Expense / Invoice / Trip, the second Task, the third Expense Report.

**4. Widen the narrow Date column** so the longer header is not truncated:

```diff
             case CONST.SEARCH.TABLE_COLUMNS.DATE:
                 columnWidth = {
-                    ...getWidthStyle(isDateColumnWide ? variables.w102 : variables.w62),
+                    // The narrow width fits the "Created" header, which is wider than the dates below it.
+                    ...getWidthStyle(isDateColumnWide ? variables.w102 : variables.w80),
                 };
```

80px is the smallest existing width variable that fits "Created" plus the sort caret. The 102px wide case is unchanged, so rows showing a past-year date are unaffected.

**Tests.** I extended `tests/unit/Search/SearchUIUtilsTest.ts` with a `Created date labels` block asserting the rendered English strings, so it is pinned to what the user sees rather than to a key name: the filter label resolves to `Created date`, `getSearchColumnTranslationKey(DATE)` and the expense header config both resolve to `Created`, and `getSortByOptions([DATE])` offers `Created`. These fail on current `main` (received `"Date"`) and pass with the change.

**Two knock-on surfaces worth an explicit decision before I open the PR**, both of which fall out of shared code rather than being separate changes:

- The single-report transaction table reuses `getExpenseHeaders()`, so its Date header renames too: https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7242015486fbde102ab7a6b470ce4e89efae433e/src/components/MoneyRequestReportView/MoneyRequestReportTableHeader.tsx#L42-L44 . I have kept it renamed on purpose, since the same column reading "Created" on Spend and "Date" one click deeper is exactly the ambiguity this issue is about. If design wants Spend-only, the header lists take a flag and I will scope it.
- `getSearchColumnTranslationKey` also builds the CSV export column labels: https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7242015486fbde102ab7a6b470ce4e89efae433e/src/hooks/useSearchBulkActions.ts#L823-L825 . Exports will therefore carry a "Created" header instead of "Date". That keeps "Export current view" matching the view, but it is a visible change for anyone with an existing import mapping, so please confirm it is wanted.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

Changing `common.date` itself to "Created date". Rejected: that key is shared with the expense date field, date of birth, travel details and the CSV import mapper, so it would rename unrelated UI across the app.

Changing only the three `SearchTableHeader.tsx` entries. Rejected: it leaves the "Edit columns" picker and the Sort by menu still calling that column "Date", because those read `getSearchColumnTranslationKey` instead.

Reusing a single `created` key for both the filter and the column. Rejected: the issue asks for two different strings ("Created date" for the filter, "Created" for the column), and one key cannot carry both. Two keys also let translators pick the right form per surface, which matters where the noun and the date phrase differ, for example `Erstellt` versus `Erstellungsdatum` in German.

priorProposals.body:
## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.

The August 2026 product update needs a persistent bottom-right product marketing window, reusing the pattern built for the July update in issue #95791. There are two audience variants: admins should see "Enhanced vendor mapping" with a Try it out button that leads them to enable (or use) Vendors on their active admin workspace, and employees should see "Pre-built agents for you" with a Try it out button that opens the new-agent flow at `settings/agents/new`.

### What is the root cause of that problem?

This is a new feature request rather than a bug. The persistent window system built for #95791 is intentionally config-driven: exactly one announcement is active at a time, defined by `ACTIVE_PRODUCT_MARKETING_ANNOUNCEMENT` in `ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts`, and it currently still holds the July 2026 update (`productUpdateJuly2026`) with an admin-only variant:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1e9d3c3ef392d36aac215f5a93bc54f047211c59/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L52-L66

No August announcement has been authored yet, so nothing new is shown. Additionally, the announcement's CTA route builder currently only receives the target admin workspace ID, which is not enough for the August admin CTA — that CTA must branch on whether the workspace's Vendors feature is already enabled:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1e9d3c3ef392d36aac215f5a93bc54f047211c59/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L36-L37

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

Replace the active announcement in `ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts` with an August 2026 announcement using a new update key (for example `productUpdateAugust2026`). Because dismissal is tracked by comparing the update key against the `lastDismissedMarketingWindow` NVP, users who dismissed the July window will automatically see the August one — no changes to the dismissal, targeting, or visibility logic are needed:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1e9d3c3ef392d36aac215f5a93bc54f047211c59/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L68-L86

**Admin variant** — heading "Enhanced vendor mapping", body "Create vendors and custom rules for easy mapping to major accounting packages.", CTA "Try it out". The CTA should navigate to the Vendors page (`workspaces/<policyID>/vendors`, the existing `WORKSPACE_VENDORS` route) when the target workspace's Vendors feature is already on, and otherwise to the More features page (`workspaces/<policyID>/more-features`, the existing `WORKSPACE_MORE_FEATURES` route) where the admin can turn Vendors on. Whether Vendors is on is exactly what the existing `hasVendorFeature` helper answers (vendor-matching beta plus a supported accounting connection), the same check the More features page uses for its Vendors toggle:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1e9d3c3ef392d36aac215f5a93bc54f047211c59/src/libs/PolicyUtils.ts#L2438-L2443

To support that branch, extend the announcement variant's CTA route builder so it receives the resolved target admin workspace's full policy object and the vendor-matching beta state, not just the workspace ID. `ProductMarketingWindowManager` already holds the full active admin policy objects (it currently narrows them down to `targetAdminPolicyID`), and it can read the beta via the existing permissions hook, so it passes both into the route builder:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1e9d3c3ef392d36aac215f5a93bc54f047211c59/src/components/ProductMarketingWindow/ProductMarketingWindowManager.tsx#L67-L68

The existing target-workspace selection already implements "their active workspace they are an admin on" (the active policy when the user is an admin on it, otherwise their first active admin workspace), so it is kept as is.

**Member (employee) variant** — heading "Pre-built agents for you", body "Use pre-built or custom agents to code, split, and submit expenses automatically on your behalf.", CTA "Try it out" navigating to the existing `SETTINGS_AGENTS_NEW` route (`settings/agents/new`), which matches the URL requested in the issue. The member variant is already optional in the announcement type and the manager already falls back to it for users with no active admin workspace, so adding it is pure configuration:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1e9d3c3ef392d36aac215f5a93bc54f047211c59/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L40-L50

**Copy and translations** — add the August heading/body/CTA strings for both variants under the existing `productMarketingWindow` namespace in `en.ts`, remove the now-unused July keys, and generate the other locales the standard way.

**Visuals** — the window's visual field already accepts either a bundled marketing image or an existing app illustration. Once the design mocks land (vendor-list image for the admin case, agents-list image for the employee case), add them as bundled assets the same way the July promo image was added; until then an existing relevant illustration can serve as the interim visual so the window is fully functional for review.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

Building the August window as a second, parallel announcement alongside the July one was ruled out — the system is deliberately single-active with no stacking or queueing, and replacing the active announcement is the intended release mechanism. Always sending the admin CTA to the More features page (skipping the vendors-enabled branch) was also ruled out because the issue explicitly asks for the direct destination when Vendors is already on.

priorProposals.body:
## Proposal

### What is the root cause of that problem?

The persistent bottom-right product marketing window system already exists (built in #95791 and driven by the dismissed-product-training NVP, e.g. the `DismissedProductTraining` selector pattern used for other banners):

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/pages/workspace/rules/PolicyRulesPageRevamp.tsx#L75-L79

There is simply no window definition for the August update, so neither the admin "Enhanced vendor mapping" card nor the employee "Pre-built agents" card renders, and their two "Try it out" destinations are not wired.

The admin CTA is also non-trivial because its target depends on whether the admin's workspace can even reach Vendors. Vendors lives inside Rules, and Rules access for a workspace is gated by `canPolicyAccessFeature` (Collect needs the Rules revamp beta, otherwise Control only):

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/libs/PolicyUtils.ts#L1453-L1465

and the Vendors toggle itself is only exposed when `VENDOR_MATCHING` is enabled on the More features page:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/pages/workspace/WorkspaceMoreFeaturesPage/index.tsx#L61-L95

So a blind link to a fixed `{policyID}/more-features` would break for members who are not admins of that workspace or whose plan cannot access Rules.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

1. Register two new product-update window entries in the same persistent-window config used by #95791 (title/subtext/image/buttons per the deliverables), each dismissible via the existing `dismissProductTraining` flow used by `RulesGeneralTab`:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/pages/workspace/rules/tabs/RulesGeneralTab.tsx#L23-L49

2. Admin case "Try it out": resolve the workspace where the current user is an admin, then route through the existing More features route. Reuse `WORKSPACE_MORE_FEATURES.getRoute(policyID)` already used on that page:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/pages/workspace/WorkspaceMoreFeaturesPage/index.tsx#L353-L387

When Vendors is already on for that workspace, deep-link straight to the Rules Vendors screen instead of More features:

```ts
const canAccessRules = canPolicyAccessFeature(policy, CONST.POLICY.MORE_FEATURES.ARE_RULES_ENABLED, isRulesRevampEnabled);
const vendorsAlreadyOn = isVendorMatchingEnabled && canAccessRules && arePolicyRulesEnabled(policy, policyCategories, isRulesRevampEnabled);
Navigation.navigate(vendorsAlreadyOn ? ROUTES.WORKSPACE_RULES.getRoute(policyID) : ROUTES.WORKSPACE_MORE_FEATURES.getRoute(policyID));
```

This mirrors the exact enablement checks in `useControlOnlyRuleUpgradeRedirect`, so the CTA never lands a member on a page their plan cannot use:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/hooks/useControlOnlyRuleUpgradeRedirect.ts#L25-L45

3. Employee case "Try it out": navigate to the new-agent route (`/settings/agents/new`) using its `ROUTES` constant, matching the CTA behavior of the existing `AgentPromotionalBanner` in `RulesGeneralTab`.

This adds the missing window definitions and gives each CTA a destination that respects admin membership and Rules/Vendors availability.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

Always link the admin CTA to a fixed `more-features` URL and let `AccessOrNotFoundWrapper` redirect, but that flashes an inaccessible page for non-admins or non-Rules plans, so resolving the correct workspace and gate up front is cleaner.

**Reminder:** Please use plain English, be brief and avoid jargon. Feel free to use images, charts or pseudo-code if necessary. Do not post large multi-line diffs or write walls of text. Do not create PRs unless you have been hired for this job.

priorProposals.body:
## Proposal

### What is the root cause of that problem?

This is new-content work, not a code defect. The persistent bottom-right window built in #95791 is content-driven: it renders whatever `ACTIVE_PRODUCT_MARKETING_ANNOUNCEMENT` contains, and that constant is still pinned to the July 2026 announcement (admin-only, no member variant):

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L57-L66

One gap does need a small code change: the August admin CTA must branch on whether Vendors is already enabled ("more features" page vs. the direct vendors URL), but the current `getCtaRoute` contract only receives the target workspace ID, so a variant can't inspect the policy's feature state:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L36-L37

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

1. In `ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts`, replace the July announcement with a new one using a fresh `updateKey` (e.g. `productUpdateAugust2026`) so users who dismissed July see August. Fill both variants: `admin` = "Enhanced vendor mapping" with the vendor-list marketing image, `member` = "Pre-built agents for you" with the agents-list image, both with a "Try it out" CTA. New strings go under `productMarketingWindow` in `en.ts`/`es.ts` next to the existing July block:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/languages/en.ts#L10534-L10540

2. Widen `getCtaRoute` to receive the target admin `Policy` object (and the vendor-matching beta flag) instead of just the ID. The manager already resolves the full policy list, so it can pass the found policy through where it currently passes only `targetAdminPolicyID`:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/components/ProductMarketingWindow/ProductMarketingWindowManager.tsx#L67-L68

The admin variant's `getCtaRoute` then reuses the same check the More Features page uses, `hasVendorFeature`:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/libs/PolicyUtils.ts#L2438-L2442

returning `ROUTES.WORKSPACE_VENDORS.getRoute(policy.id)` when vendors are on, otherwise `ROUTES.WORKSPACE_MORE_FEATURES.getRoute(policy.id)`. The member variant's `getCtaRoute` simply returns `ROUTES.SETTINGS_AGENTS_NEW.getRoute()`. All display/dismiss/precedence logic in the manager and window component stays untouched.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

Keep `getCtaRoute(policyID)` as-is and do the vendors-enabled branch inside the manager's `completeCta`. Rejected because it leaks announcement-specific logic into the shared manager; keeping routing decisions inside the variant keeps future updates content-only.

priorProposals.author: too-ticky
priorProposals.body:
## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.

Ship the August 2026 product update persistent bottom-right window: an admin variant ("Enhanced vendor mapping") with a CTA that deep-links into that workspace's **vendors page** when Vendors is already on, or falls back to **more-features** otherwise; and an employee variant ("Pre-built agents for you") whose CTA opens `settings/agents/new` — but only for accounts that can actually reach that route.

### What is the root cause of that problem?

No August announcement exists in the config-driven system. Authoring it looks mechanical until you hit three non-obvious landmines.

**Landmine 1: `areVendorsEnabled` does not exist as a Policy field.** A grep of `src/` returns zero hits on any property named `areVendorsEnabled` or `vendorsEnabled`. Vendors enablement is a *derived* predicate:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/6ed77eddc647cb35737bdffa0f19ccce6dabf468/src/libs/PolicyUtils.ts#L2445-L2450

`hasVendorFeature` reads `policy.connections` to check whether the relevant accounting connection has `vendorMatching` active. This matters because the manager currently discards the policy object and exposes only `policy.id`:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/6ed77eddc647cb35737bdffa0f19ccce6dabf468/src/components/ProductMarketingWindow/ProductMarketingWindowManager.tsx#L66-L68

Calling `hasVendorFeature(policyID)` is a type error — calling it with only an ID and expecting a connections-derived answer returns wrong results.

**Landmine 2: Connections are only hydrated for the currently-active workspace.** `usePolicyConnectionsPrefetch` fetches connections at startup for the single active policy:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/6ed77eddc647cb35737bdffa0f19ccce6dabf468/src/hooks/usePolicyConnectionsPrefetch.ts#L22-L31

The announcement targets the *first admin workspace* when the user's active workspace is not one they admin. For that fallback workspace, `policy.connections` may be empty at render time, so `hasVendorFeature` returns `false` and every admin gets routed to more-features regardless. This is acceptable (more-features is the issue's specified default and itself prefetches connections before rendering the Vendors row), but the reasoning must be explicit — otherwise a future reviewer "fixes" the fallback with a gratuitous `openPolicyAccountingPage` call that races the prefetch.

**Landmine 3: The employee CTA dead-ends for custom-agent accounts.** `settings/agents/new` is wrapped in `withAgentAccessDenied`, which silently redirects `isCustomAgent` users to Profile:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/6ed77eddc647cb35737bdffa0f19ccce6dabf468/src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/withAgentAccessDenied.tsx#L60-L72

Custom-agent users would see the "Pre-built agents for you" card, tap the CTA, and land on their own Profile with no explanation. The window must be suppressed entirely for agent accounts, not just the CTA.

Additionally, the `VENDOR_MATCHING` beta gates Vendors visibility on more-features:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/6ed77eddc647cb35737bdffa0f19ccce6dabf468/src/pages/workspace/WorkspaceMoreFeaturesPage/index.tsx#L461-L466

An admin outside the beta who lands on more-features would see no Vendors row. That admin should fall through to the employee variant rather than receive a broken admin experience.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

**`src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts`** — widen the CTA callback's input from a bare policy ID to a context object that carries the resolved `Policy` (for `hasVendorFeature`) and a beta-check function (for routing decisions):

```ts
type ProductMarketingAnnouncementCtaContext = {
    adminPolicy?: Policy;
    isBetaEnabled: (beta: Beta) => boolean;
};
```

Register the August announcement and add the two promo images from the attached zip to `assets/images/`:

```ts
const ACTIVE_PRODUCT_MARKETING_ANNOUNCEMENT: ProductMarketingAnnouncement | null = {
    updateKey: 'productUpdateAugust2026',
    admin: {
        visual: {type: 'image', source: August26VendorsPromoImage},
        heading: 'productMarketingWindow.vendorMapping.heading',
        body:    'productMarketingWindow.vendorMapping.body',
        ctaLabel:'productMarketingWindow.vendorMapping.cta',
        getCtaRoute: ({adminPolicy, isBetaEnabled}) =>
            hasVendorFeature(adminPolicy, isBetaEnabled(CONST.BETAS.VENDOR_MATCHING))
                ? ROUTES.WORKSPACE_VENDORS.getRoute(adminPolicy?.id)
                : ROUTES.WORKSPACE_MORE_FEATURES.getRoute(adminPolicy?.id),
    },
    member: {
        visual: {type: 'image', source: August26AgentsPromoImage},
        heading: 'productMarketingWindow.agents.heading',
        body:    'productMarketingWindow.agents.body',
        ctaLabel:'productMarketingWindow.agents.cta',
        getCtaRoute: () => ROUTES.SETTINGS_AGENTS_NEW.getRoute(),
    },
};
```

**`ProductMarketingWindowManager.tsx`** — resolve the full policy object, gate the admin variant on the `VENDOR_MATCHING` beta (so out-of-beta admins see the employee card), suppress the window entirely for agent accounts, and pass context to `getCtaRoute`:

```ts
const {isBetaEnabled} = usePermissions();
const isAgentAccount = useIsAgentAccount();
const targetAdminPolicy =
    activeAdminPolicies?.find((p) => p.id === activePolicyID)
    ?? activeAdminPolicies?.at(0);
const isAdminVariant = !!targetAdminPolicy && isBetaEnabled(CONST.BETAS.VENDOR_MATCHING);
const variant = getProductMarketingAnnouncementVariant(announcement, isAdminVariant, lastDismissedMarketingWindow);
```

Early-exit before render:
```ts
if (... || isActingAsDelegate || isAgentAccount || isCoveredByCenteredModalScreen) {
```

CTA dispatch: `Navigation.navigate(variant.getCtaRoute({adminPolicy: targetAdminPolicy, isBetaEnabled}))`.

**Translations** — add `vendorMapping` and `agents` subtrees under `productMarketingWindow` in `en.ts` and every other locale (TypeScript's `TranslationPaths` enforces parity at compile time). Remove the now-dead `roleTypes.*` keys and `july26-promo.png`. Update `tests/unit/ProductMarketingWindowUtilsTest.ts` to use the new `getCtaRoute` context signature and retire the `roleTypes` fixtures.
