priorProposals.body:
## Proposal

### What is the root cause of that problem?

New Feature.

The persistent bottom-right window built in #95791 is deliberately **single-active**: exactly one announcement is defined by `ACTIVE_PRODUCT_MARKETING_ANNOUNCEMENT` in `ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts`, dismissal is keyed on its `updateKey` (compared against the `NVP_LAST_DISMISSED_MARKETING_WINDOW` NVP), and it currently still holds the **July** update with an admin-only variant — so nothing new renders:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1df21965ec26cee4e5d2dc0e1e2a6b1483a2cdb2/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L57-L66

The one structural gap for August is the admin CTA. The variant's route builder only receives the workspace ID — [`ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L36-L37`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1df21965ec26cee4e5d2dc0e1e2a6b1483a2cdb2/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L36-L37) — which is not enough to branch on whether Vendors is already on for that workspace, as the "if Vendors is turned on, take them to the direct URL" deliverable requires.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

**Replace the active announcement** in `ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts` with an August one under a new key (e.g. `productUpdateAugust2026`). Because dismissal compares `updateKey` against the NVP, users who dismissed July automatically see August — the visibility, targeting, and dismissal logic at [`ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L84-L86`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1df21965ec26cee4e5d2dc0e1e2a6b1483a2cdb2/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L84-L86) is unchanged.

**Widen `getCtaRoute` to one context object** — `(ctx: {policyID?: string; policy?: OnyxEntry<Policy>; isVendorMatchingBetaEnabled?: boolean}) => Route`. The member variant just ignores the fields it doesn't need, so a single shape covers both. This builder has exactly one caller and one definition site (below), so the signature change touches only those two places.

**Admin variant** — heading `Enhanced vendor mapping`, body `Create vendors and custom rules for easy mapping to major accounting packages.`, CTA `Try it out`. Its `getCtaRoute` returns `WORKSPACE_VENDORS.getRoute(policyID)` when Vendors is on, else `WORKSPACE_MORE_FEATURES.getRoute(policyID)`. "Vendors is on" is exactly `hasVendorFeature(policy, isVendorMatchingBetaEnabled)` (vendor-matching beta + a supported accounting connection) — the same predicate the More features page uses for its Vendors toggle, so the CTA and the toggle agree:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1df21965ec26cee4e5d2dc0e1e2a6b1483a2cdb2/src/libs/PolicyUtils.ts#L2445-L2450

[`WorkspaceMoreFeaturesPage/index.tsx#L461-L466`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1df21965ec26cee4e5d2dc0e1e2a6b1483a2cdb2/src/pages/workspace/WorkspaceMoreFeaturesPage/index.tsx#L461-L466)

**In `ProductMarketingWindowManager`**, pass that context. It already holds the full active-admin policy objects (it currently narrows them to the ID at [`#L67-L68`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1df21965ec26cee4e5d2dc0e1e2a6b1483a2cdb2/src/components/ProductMarketingWindow/ProductMarketingWindowManager.tsx#L67-L68)) and can read the beta with `usePermissions().isBetaEnabled(CONST.BETAS.VENDOR_MATCHING)`, so the CTA call becomes `variant.getCtaRoute({policyID: targetAdminPolicyID, policy: targetAdminPolicy, isVendorMatchingBetaEnabled})`:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1df21965ec26cee4e5d2dc0e1e2a6b1483a2cdb2/src/components/ProductMarketingWindow/ProductMarketingWindowManager.tsx#L87

**Member (employee) variant** — heading `Pre-built agents for you`, body `Use pre-built or custom agents to code, split, and submit expenses automatically on your behalf.`, CTA `Try it out`, `getCtaRoute` returning `SETTINGS_AGENTS_NEW.getRoute()` (its object-arg signature yields `settings/agents/new` with no `policyID`), matching the requested URL. The variant is already optional in the type and the manager already falls back to it for users with no active admin workspace, so this is pure config.

**Copy** — under the existing `productMarketingWindow.roleTypes` namespace, update `admin.heading`/`admin.body` and add a `member` sub-object; `cta` stays `Try it out` (no new CTA string), then generate `es` + all locales:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1df21965ec26cee4e5d2dc0e1e2a6b1483a2cdb2/src/languages/en.ts#L10498-L10506

**Visuals** — add the two bundled promo images from the attached `promo images.zip` the same way `July26PromoImage` is imported at the top of the utils file, one per variant.

**Caveat worth stating:** `hasVendorFeature` reads `policy.connections`, which this window (unlike the More features page's `usePolicyConnectionsPrefetch`) never prefetches. If the target workspace's connections aren't in Onyx yet, it returns `false` and the admin CTA routes to **more-features** — which is precisely the spec's default destination, so the fallback is safe rather than wrong.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

- **The `dismissProductTraining` / product-training NVP approach** (register two window entries, gate the admin link on `canPolicyAccessFeature` + the Rules-revamp beta) — this is the wrong subsystem: the persistent window is the single-active `ACTIVE_PRODUCT_MARKETING_ANNOUNCEMENT`, dismissed via `NVP_LAST_DISMISSED_MARKETING_WINDOW`, which does not stack or queue; and "Vendors on" is `hasVendorFeature`, not Rules access.
- **Extending `getCtaRoute` with extra positional args** (policy + beta alongside the ID) works, but a single context object keeps the member variant — which needs none of them — from carrying unused parameters, and leaves room for future variants.
- **A second, parallel announcement alongside July** — ruled out; the system is single-active by design, and replacing the active announcement is the intended release mechanism.

priorProposals.body:
# Proposal

## Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.
We need to author the content for the **August 2026 product update** in the existing "persistent bottom-right product marketing window" (first built for issue #95791), with two audience-targeted variants:
- **Admin variant** — "Enhanced vendor mapping": title, subtext, a vendor/accounting-packages image, and a "Try it out" CTA that opens the admin's active workspace's More Features page (`workspaces/:policyID/more-features`) — unless the Vendors feature is already turned on for that workspace, in which case it should go straight to the Vendors page.
- **Employee variant** — "Pre-built agents for you": title, subtext, an agents-list image, and a "Try it out" CTA that opens `new.expensify.com/settings/agents/new`.

## What is the root cause of that problem?
This isn't a bug — it's a content/config change to a feature that already exists and is architected exactly for this: swap in a new announcement. Nothing needs to be built from scratch; we need to (a) replace the single active announcement's content/CTA data, and (b) extend the CTA-resolution logic just enough to support the admin variant's conditional destination.

**Where the current (July 2026) announcement lives — this is the single source of truth for content, per-audience variants, and CTA routing:**
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c926b197/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L57-L66

Today `ACTIVE_PRODUCT_MARKETING_ANNOUNCEMENT` only defines an `admin` variant (no `member` variant), and `admin.getCtaRoute` is a simple one-line route builder that ignores any feature state — it just forwards the admin policy ID into `ROUTES.WORKSPACE_MEMBERS.getRoute`. The type only allows `getCtaRoute` to receive an `adminPolicyID`:
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c926b197/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L23-L38

That's the gap: our new admin CTA must branch ("Vendors already on?" → Vendors page, else → More Features page), but there's currently no way to pass that "is the feature already on" signal into `getCtaRoute`.

**Where the variant is resolved and the CTA is actually invoked** — this is where the target admin policy is already computed, and where the extra "is Vendors on" signal needs to be assembled and threaded through:
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c926b197/src/components/ProductMarketingWindow/ProductMarketingWindowManager.tsx#L47-L98
Specifically, `targetAdminPolicyID` (line 67) is derived from the full policy objects already fetched via `activeAdminPolicies` (line 49-51), and `completeCta` (lines 84-88) is what calls `variant.getCtaRoute(targetAdminPolicyID)` before navigating.

**The "is Vendors on" check already exists and is exactly the right function to reuse** — it's the same predicate that drives the (currently locked) Vendors toggle on the More Features page, checking whether a supported accounting integration (QBO/Intacct/Xero) is connected in vendor-matching mode, gated behind the `vendorMatching` beta:
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c926b197/src/libs/PolicyUtils.ts#L2445-L2450
It's consumed the same way in `WorkspaceMoreFeaturesPage`:
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c926b197/src/pages/workspace/WorkspaceMoreFeaturesPage/index.tsx#L461-L479

For the employee variant's destination, `settings/agents/new` already exists as `ROUTES.SETTINGS_AGENTS_NEW`:
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c926b197/src/ROUTES.ts#L2003-L2012

One more relevant fact: the "custom agents" feature is still beta-gated elsewhere in the app (e.g. the AI features promo modal only shows its "Build your own agents" page when `CONST.BETAS.CUSTOM_AGENT` is enabled for the account):
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c926b197/src/components/AIFeaturesPromoModal.tsx#L26-L27
`NewAgentPage` itself (behind `SETTINGS_AGENTS_NEW`) does not re-check that beta, so a non-beta employee who clicks "Try it out" would land on a page that isn't really meant for them yet — the marketing window should not advertise this to accounts without the beta, mirroring how the rest of the app treats this feature as opt-in.

## What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

**1. Add the new images as static assets**, analogous to the existing `assets/images/july26-promo.png` import at the top of `ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts` (line 1) — one for the vendor-mapping admin visual, one for the pre-built-agents employee visual (sourced from the "promo images.zip" attached to this issue).

**2. Replace `ACTIVE_PRODUCT_MARKETING_ANNOUNCEMENT`** in
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c926b197/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L57-L66
with a new entry using a fresh `updateKey` (e.g. `'productUpdateAugust2026'` — must be new so it isn't treated as already-dismissed by users who dismissed July's window), defining both `admin` and `member` variants with the copy from the issue, and CTA routes:

```ts
admin: {
    visual: {type: 'image', source: Aug26VendorMappingPromoImage},
    heading: 'productMarketingWindow.roleTypes.admin.heading',
    body: 'productMarketingWindow.roleTypes.admin.body',
    ctaLabel: 'productMarketingWindow.roleTypes.admin.cta',
    getCtaRoute: (adminPolicyID, isVendorFeatureActive) =>
        isVendorFeatureActive ? ROUTES.WORKSPACE_VENDORS.getRoute(adminPolicyID) : ROUTES.WORKSPACE_MORE_FEATURES.getRoute(adminPolicyID),
},
member: {
    visual: {type: 'image', source: Aug26AgentsPromoImage},
    heading: 'productMarketingWindow.roleTypes.member.heading',
    body: 'productMarketingWindow.roleTypes.member.body',
    ctaLabel: 'productMarketingWindow.roleTypes.member.cta',
    getCtaRoute: () => ROUTES.SETTINGS_AGENTS_NEW.getRoute(),
},
```

**3. Widen the `getCtaRoute` signature by one optional param** in the same file so the admin variant can branch on feature state:
```ts
getCtaRoute: (adminPolicyID?: string, isVendorFeatureActive?: boolean) => Route;
```
This is additive and backward-compatible — existing test doubles in `tests/unit/ProductMarketingWindowUtilsTest.ts` and `tests/unit/ProductMarketingWindowTest.tsx` define `getCtaRoute` with zero or one argument, which remains a valid implementation of the widened function type (TypeScript allows an implementation to ignore trailing params).

**4. In `ProductMarketingWindowManager.tsx`**, compute the two new pieces of eligibility state alongside the existing `usePermissions`-style hooks and pass them through:
- Resolve the full target admin `Policy` object (the manager already finds it via `activeAdminPolicies.find(...)` at line 67 to get the ID — reuse the same lookup to keep the object, not just the ID).
- Add `const {isBetaEnabled} = usePermissions();` and compute `isVendorFeatureActive = hasVendorFeature(targetAdminPolicy, isBetaEnabled(CONST.BETAS.VENDOR_MATCHING))`, importing `hasVendorFeature` from `@user/PolicyUtils`.
- Pass it into the CTA call: `Navigation.navigate(variant.getCtaRoute(targetAdminPolicyID, isVendorFeatureActive))` (line 87).
- Gate the employee/member variant on `isBetaEnabled(CONST.BETAS.CUSTOM_AGENT)`: when the resolved audience is "member" (not admin) and this beta is disabled, treat the announcement as having no eligible variant for that user (hide the window), the same way `getProductMarketingAnnouncementVariant` already hides the window when there's no `member` variant defined at all. Concretely, this means passing an extra `isMemberVariantEligible` boolean into `getProductMarketingAnnouncementVariant` in `ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts` (https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c926b197/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L77-L86) and returning `undefined` instead of `announcement.member` when it's false.

**5. Add the translation keys** under `productMarketingWindow.roleTypes` in `src/languages/en.ts` (and other locale files), following the existing shape at
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c926b197/src/languages/en.ts#L10498-L10506
adding a sibling `member` (or `employee`) key next to `admin`, each with `heading`, `body`, and `cta` using the exact copy given in the issue.

### Edge cases handled
- **Vendors beta/integration not enabled for the target workspace**: `hasVendorFeature` already returns `false` unless the `vendorMatching` beta is on *and* a supported integration is connected in vendor-matching mode, so the CTA correctly falls back to the More Features page instead of a Vendors page the admin can't act on.
- **Non-beta employees**: gating the member variant on `CONST.BETAS.CUSTOM_AGENT` prevents advertising agents to accounts where the feature isn't available yet, consistent with how `AIFeaturesPromoModal` already treats this beta.
- **Loading state**: `ProductMarketingWindowManager` already blocks rendering until `activeAdminPoliciesMetadata` (and friends) finish loading before computing `targetAdminPolicyID`/variant, so the new `hasVendorFeature` check (which depends on `policy.connections`, part of the same policy object) isn't evaluated against stale/partial data.
- **Offline**: no new network calls are introduced; `hasVendorFeature` and `isBetaEnabled` are both pure/local reads of already-synced Onyx data, same as the existing admin-vs-member resolution.
- **Web/iOS/Android**: no new platform-specific code paths — the window's rendering, portal, and styling are unchanged; only the content and CTA-route data change.
- **Existing callers**: `getCtaRoute`'s widened signature doesn't break the July-2026 admin variant's shape (it's being replaced wholesale) nor the unit/UI test mocks, since the added parameter is optional and appended at the end.
- **Dismissal**: using a brand-new `updateKey` ensures users who already dismissed the July 2026 window still see the new August window (per the existing single-slot, no-fallthrough dismissal design already documented at lines 52-56 of `ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts`).

newProposal.body:
## Proposal

### What is the root cause of that problem?

Opening `/v/1/1` renders `ValidateCodeModal`, and since "1" is not a valid 6-digit magic code, it shows the full-page "not found" view. That view's "Go back to home page" link is overridden to call a plain `Navigation.goBack()` with no fallback route:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/components/ValidateCode/ValidateCodeModal.tsx#L44-L52

But when a `/v/...` link is opened directly, `VALIDATE_LOGIN` is deliberately built as the only route in the root stack — no tab navigator is prepended underneath it:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/libs/Navigation/helpers/getAdaptedStateFromPath.ts#L56-L63

So there is nothing to go back to: `goBack()` hits the `canGoBack()` guard, logs "Unable to go back", and returns without doing anything — the button appears dead:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/libs/Navigation/Navigation.ts#L560-L563

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

Remove the `onLinkPress` override in `ValidateCodeModal` so `FullPageNotFoundView` uses its default handler, `Navigation.goBackToHome()`:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/components/BlockingViews/FullPageNotFoundView.tsx#L84

`goBackToHome()` calls `goBack(ROUTES.HOME)`, and when Home isn't in the stack, `goUp` replaces the lone `/v/` route with the tab navigator instead of no-opping — landing signed-in users on Home and signed-out users on the sign-in page, which matches the link's label. When the page was reached from within the app it still pops back normally.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

Keep the override but pass a fallback route — `Navigation.goBack(ROUTES.HOME)` — which pops when history exists and replaces with Home when the `/v/` route is the stack root. The same fallback could be applied to the header back button shown on narrow layouts, which no-ops for the same reason.

note: Withdrawn in production with seven priors, and the match is not the first or the last of them.

## Proposal

### What is the root cause of that problem?

`/v/1/1` resolves to the `VALIDATE_LOGIN: 'v/:accountID/:validateCode'` route ([`ROUTES.ts#L62`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/3f4e1a173b6b0e8b538c077cfef1d7af082e3659/src/ROUTES.ts#L62)), so `validateCode` is `'1'`. `isValidValidateCode('1')` is `false` ([`ValidationUtils.ts#L373-L375`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/3f4e1a173b6b0e8b538c077cfef1d7af082e3659/src/libs/ValidationUtils.ts#L373-L375)), so `ValidateCodeModal` renders `FullPageNotFoundView` with `shouldShow`, i.e. the "Hmm... it's not here" page and its **Go back to home page** link ([`ValidateCodeModal.tsx#L41-L52`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/3f4e1a173b6b0e8b538c077cfef1d7af082e3659/src/components/ValidateCode/ValidateCodeModal.tsx#L41-L52)).

That link's handler is overridden with a bare `Navigation.goBack()` — with **no fallback route** — here:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/3f4e1a173b6b0e8b538c077cfef1d7af082e3659/src/components/ValidateCode/ValidateCodeModal.tsx#L49-L51

This override was added together with the not-found page itself in PR #52407. Opening `/v/1/1` directly is a fresh entry with no in-app navigation stack, so inside `goBack` the guard `!backToRoute && !shouldPopToSidebar && !navigationRef.current?.canGoBack()` is true — it logs `[Navigation] Unable to go back` and returns without navigating ([`Navigation.ts#L560-L563`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/3f4e1a173b6b0e8b538c077cfef1d7af082e3659/src/libs/Navigation/Navigation.ts#L560-L563)). The button does nothing.

The override replaced a default that already handled this correctly: `FullPageNotFoundView`'s own default is `onLinkPress = () => Navigation.goBackToHome()` ([`FullPageNotFoundView.tsx#L84`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/3f4e1a173b6b0e8b538c077cfef1d7af082e3659/src/components/BlockingViews/FullPageNotFoundView.tsx#L84)), and `goBackToHome` calls `goBack(ROUTES.HOME)` ([`Navigation.ts#L674-L687`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/3f4e1a173b6b0e8b538c077cfef1d7af082e3659/src/libs/Navigation/Navigation.ts#L674-L687)) — `backToRoute` is set, so the `canGoBack` guard is bypassed and it navigates Home even with no history. This is why the **Go back to home page button is not responsive**.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

**Primary fix (root cause):** Remove the `onLinkPress` override at [`ValidateCodeModal.tsx#L49-L51`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/3f4e1a173b6b0e8b538c077cfef1d7af082e3659/src/components/ValidateCode/ValidateCodeModal.tsx#L49-L51) so the component falls back to `FullPageNotFoundView`'s default `Navigation.goBackToHome()`. That default passes `ROUTES.HOME`, so it works with no history and matches the link's own "Go back to home page" label ([`goBackHome` string](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/3f4e1a173b6b0e8b538c077cfef1d7af082e3659/src/languages/en.ts#L3726)). It is safe because Home is exactly what the label promises, so navigating Home unconditionally is the intended behavior even on the rare path where history exists — no regression.

**Adjacent coverage:** On narrow layout the same page shows a header back button (`shouldShowBackButton={shouldUseNarrowLayout}`) whose `onBackButtonPress` is the identical fallback-less default `() => Navigation.goBack()` ([`FullPageNotFoundView.tsx#L81`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/3f4e1a173b6b0e8b538c077cfef1d7af082e3659/src/components/BlockingViews/FullPageNotFoundView.tsx#L81)), so on mWeb it is broken the same way. Pass `onBackButtonPress={() => Navigation.goBackToHome()}` on the same `FullPageNotFoundView` so the whole not-found screen is fixed, not only the reported link.

<details>
<summary>Verification (web) — reproduced and fixed</summary>

Navigated directly to `/v/1/1`: the link click left the URL at `/v/1/1` (no-op). After removing the override, the same click navigated to `/home`.
</details>

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

- **`onLinkPress={() => Navigation.goBack(ROUTES.HOME)}`** (keep the override, add a fallback) — functionally equivalent since `goBackToHome` wraps `goBack(ROUTES.HOME)`, but removing the override is cleaner and restores the component's own tested default rather than reimplementing it.
- **Give `goBack()` a global Home fallback when `canGoBack()` is false** — too broad; it changes behavior for every `goBack()` caller in the app, whereas the defect is local to this one overridden handler.

priorProposals.body:
## Proposal

### What is the root cause of that problem?

`/v/1/1` maps to the magic-link route [`VALIDATE_LOGIN: 'v/:accountID/:validateCode'`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/ROUTES.ts#L62), so `accountID=1`, `validateCode=1`. On web, `ValidateLoginPage` renders `ValidateCodeModal` for this state (no sign-in flow starts because the code is invalid) — see [`index.web.tsx:174-179`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/pages/ValidateLoginPage/index.web.tsx#L174-L179). `isValidValidateCode('1')` is `false`, so `ValidateCodeModal`'s `FullPageNotFoundView` shows the "Hmm... it's not here" page with the **Go back to home page** link ([`ValidateCodeModal.tsx:41-52`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/components/ValidateCode/ValidateCodeModal.tsx#L41-L52)).

The dead button is that link's handler. `ValidateCodeModal` overrides `onLinkPress` with a bare `Navigation.goBack()` and passes **no fallback route** at [`ValidateCodeModal.tsx:49-51`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/components/ValidateCode/ValidateCodeModal.tsx#L49-L51). When you open `/v/1/1` directly (fresh tab, no in-app navigation history), `goBack()` with no `backToRoute` hits the guard at [`Navigation.ts:560-563`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/libs/Navigation/Navigation.ts#L560-L563): `navigationRef.canGoBack()` is `false`, so it logs `[Navigation] Unable to go back` and returns without navigating. The link does nothing.

The override is what breaks it. `FullPageNotFoundView`'s own default already handles this correctly — [`FullPageNotFoundView.tsx:84`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/components/BlockingViews/FullPageNotFoundView.tsx#L84) defaults `onLinkPress` to `Navigation.goBackToHome()`, which calls `goBack(ROUTES.HOME)` ([`Navigation.ts:674-687`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/libs/Navigation/Navigation.ts#L674-L687)) and, because it passes a `backToRoute`, dispatches a NAVIGATE to Home regardless of history. `ValidateCodeModal` throws that fallback away.

This is why it's so visible on desktop specifically: `shouldShowBackButton={shouldUseNarrowLayout}` ([`ValidateCodeModal.tsx:48`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/components/ValidateCode/ValidateCodeModal.tsx#L48)) hides the header back button on wide layout, so the "Go back to home page" link is the *only* exit — and it's the dead one.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

Component/render layer, in [`ValidateCodeModal.tsx`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/components/ValidateCode/ValidateCodeModal.tsx#L49-L51).

I'd just **remove the `onLinkPress` override** and let `FullPageNotFoundView`'s default `Navigation.goBackToHome()` run. That matches the link's own label (`notFound.goBackHome` → "Go back to home page"), and `goBackToHome()` also handles the narrow-layout double-pop that a bare `goBack(ROUTES.HOME)` wouldn't.

If we want to keep the "go back if there's history, else Home" intent instead, pass a fallback: `onLinkPress={() => Navigation.goBack(ROUTES.HOME)}`. Either fixes the dead button; I prefer removing the override since it's less code and the default is exactly what's wanted here.

One adjacent note: on narrow layout the header back button uses the same fallback-less default (`onBackButtonPress = () => Navigation.goBack()`, [`FullPageNotFoundView.tsx:81`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/components/BlockingViews/FullPageNotFoundView.tsx#L81)), so if we care about mWeb here too, it should get a Home fallback as well. The reported repro is wide-layout desktop, where that button is hidden, so it isn't strictly required for this ticket.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

- **Fix the shared link handler in `FullPageNotFoundView`/`BlockingView` instead.** Rejected: the shared default is already correct — `onLinkPress = () => Navigation.goBackToHome()` works on every other not-found page. Only `ValidateCodeModal` overrides it, so this is page-specific, not a shared-component bug.
- **Treat this as a routing problem (`/v/1/1` shouldn't land here / `accountID=1` is special).** Rejected: the route mapping and the page are behaving correctly — an invalid code *should* render the not-found interstitial. The rendering is right; only the link's navigation handler is wrong. Changing routing would mask a correct render path.

## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.

Opening `/v/1/1` (or any `/v/:accountID/:validateCode` link with an invalid code) directly in a fresh tab shows the "Hmm... it's not here" page, and clicking **Go back to home page** does nothing — the URL stays on `/v/1/1`.

### What is the root cause of that problem?

`/v/:accountID/:validateCode` renders [`ValidateCodeModal`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/components/ValidateCode/ValidateCodeModal.tsx#L43-L52), which shows `FullPageNotFoundView` when the code fails `isValidValidateCode`.

`FullPageNotFoundView` already ships a correct default for its link — [`onLinkPress = () => Navigation.goBackToHome()`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/components/BlockingViews/FullPageNotFoundView.tsx#L84), and `goBackToHome()` calls [`goBack(ROUTES.HOME)`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/libs/Navigation/Navigation.ts#L674-L678) with an explicit HOME fallback, so it works even with no history.

But `ValidateCodeModal` overrides that with a bare [`Navigation.goBack()`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/components/ValidateCode/ValidateCodeModal.tsx#L49-L51) with no fallback route. When the page is opened as a fresh deep link there is no navigation history, so `goBack()` hits the [`canGoBack()` guard](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/libs/Navigation/Navigation.ts#L560-L563), logs `Unable to go back`, and returns without navigating. The button appears unresponsive.

The same applies to the narrow-layout header back button: `FullPageNotFoundView`'s `onBackButtonPress` also defaults to a fallback-less `Navigation.goBack()`.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

Drop the override so the component's own correct default (`goBackToHome()`) is used:

```
<FullPageNotFoundView
    testID="validate-code-not-found"
    shouldShow={!isValidCode}
    shouldForceFullScreen={!isValidCode}
    shouldShowBackButton={shouldUseNarrowLayout}
>
```

That restores the Home fallback and matches the "Go back to home page" label.

To also fix the narrow-layout header back button (same class of bug), pass a HOME fallback in `FullPageNotFoundView`:

```
onBackButtonPress = () => Navigation.goBackToHome(),
```

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

Keep the override but give it a fallback: `onLinkPress={() => Navigation.goBack(ROUTES.HOME)}`. Works, but re-implements what `goBackToHome()` already does, so removing the override is cleaner.

## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.

Opening the magic-link validation URL directly on web — e.g. `https://staging.new.expensify.com/v/1/1` — shows the "Hmm... it's not here" page, and clicking **Go back to home page** does nothing. The URL stays at `/v/1/1`. Reproduces on staging and production, wide layout (Windows Chrome).

### What is the root cause of that problem?

`/v/1/1` matches `VALIDATE_LOGIN: 'v/:accountID/:validateCode'` ([`ROUTES.ts:62`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/ROUTES.ts#L62)), so `validateCode = "1"`. That fails `isValidValidateCode`, so `ValidateCodeModal` renders `FullPageNotFoundView` with `shouldShow` — the not-found page with the **Go back to home page** link.

`ValidateCodeModal` overrides that link's handler with a bare `Navigation.goBack()` and **no** `backToRoute` ([`ValidateCodeModal.tsx:49-51`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/components/ValidateCode/ValidateCodeModal.tsx#L49-L51)). When you land on `/v/1/1` in a fresh tab there is no in-app history, so inside `goBack` the branch at [`Navigation.ts:560-563`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/libs/Navigation/Navigation.ts#L560-L563) fires: `!backToRoute && !shouldPopToSidebar && !navigationRef.current?.canGoBack()` → it logs `[Navigation] Unable to go back` and returns without navigating. The link is dead.

The component's own default handler already does the right thing — [`FullPageNotFoundView.tsx:84`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/components/BlockingViews/FullPageNotFoundView.tsx#L84) sets `onLinkPress = () => Navigation.goBackToHome()`, and `goBackToHome` calls `goBack(ROUTES.HOME)` ([`Navigation.ts:674-686`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/libs/Navigation/Navigation.ts#L674-L686)). Because `backToRoute` is now truthy, the no-history guard is skipped and navigation runs via the `goUp(backToRoute)` branch. The override is the only thing breaking the link — it discards the fallback route the default supplies.

(There's a latent sibling on narrow layout: `shouldShowBackButton={shouldUseNarrowLayout}` is set, and the header back button falls through to `FullPageNotFoundView`'s default `onBackButtonPress = () => Navigation.goBack()` at [line 81](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/components/BlockingViews/FullPageNotFoundView.tsx#L81) — same fallback-less shape. That default is global to every not-found page, so I'm leaving it out of scope; the reported wide-layout symptom is the link.)

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

One change — delete the `onLinkPress` override in `ValidateCodeModal` so the link uses `FullPageNotFoundView`'s default `goBackToHome()`:

```diff
         <FullPageNotFoundView
             testID="validate-code-not-found"
             shouldShow={!isValidCode}
             shouldForceFullScreen={!isValidCode}
             shouldShowBackButton={shouldUseNarrowLayout}
-            onLinkPress={() => {
-                Navigation.goBack();
-            }}
         >
```

**Layer:** render/props — the bug is a prop override at the call site, not in `Navigation` or `FullPageNotFoundView`, so the fix belongs at the call site.

**Minimality:** this is the whole fix. The override is necessary and sufficient as the cause — it's the only thing shadowing the working default, and the default (`goBackToHome` → `goBack(ROUTES.HOME)`) passes an explicit route that bypasses the `!canGoBack()` guard. Removing it also makes the handler match the link's label ("Go back to home page").

**Precedent:** the codebase already uses an explicit `ROUTES.HOME` fallback for exactly the "not-found page with possibly no history" case — [`NotFoundPage.tsx:56`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/50938ee687c87107298f20d36e24a6e300f7e0d2/src/pages/ErrorPage/NotFoundPage.tsx#L56) passes `() => Navigation.goBack(ROUTES.HOME)`. Removing the override restores the same guarantee via the named `goBackToHome` helper.

**Edge cases:** signed-out users on this page navigate to `ROUTES.HOME` (the public flow), which is the intended "go home" behavior and identical to the default everywhere else. No offline/optimistic concerns — it's a pure navigation call.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

I considered making `goBack()` itself fall back to `ROUTES.HOME` when `canGoBack()` is false. I rejected it: the `!canGoBack()` early-return and its `[Navigation] Unable to go back` log at `Navigation.ts:560-563` are relied on app-wide, and forcing a Home navigation there would change behavior for every `goBack()` caller. The fault is local to this one override, so the fix should be too.

Keeping the override but adding the route — `onLinkPress={() => Navigation.goBack(ROUTES.HOME)}` — also works and mirrors `NotFoundPage.tsx:56` verbatim. I prefer deleting the override because the default is already this, and `goBackToHome()` documents the intent that the link's label states.

priorProposals.body:
## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.

Opening a magic sign-in link with an invalid code (for example https://staging.new.expensify.com/v/1/1) shows the "Hmm... it's not here" page, but clicking its "Go back to home page" button does nothing — the user stays stuck on the not-found page.

### What is the root cause of that problem?

The `/v/:accountID/:validateCode` route renders `ValidateCodeModal`, and because the code `1` fails the six-digit validation, the modal shows a full-screen `FullPageNotFoundView`. That view's "Go back to home page" link is wired to a plain `Navigation.goBack()` here:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/af37ee85da464d76cc6a95a0fa9c9414dc7f2b8c/src/components/ValidateCode/ValidateCodeModal.tsx#L44-L52

When the link is opened directly in a browser tab (which is how magic-link URLs are always reached), the `/v/` route is the only entry in the root navigation stack. `Navigation.goBack()` explicitly bails out when there is no screen to go back to — it just logs "Unable to go back" and returns:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/af37ee85da464d76cc6a95a0fa9c9414dc7f2b8c/src/libs/Navigation/Navigation.ts#L560-L563

So the press handler runs, does nothing, and the button appears unresponsive.

The codebase already documents this exact pitfall for this exact route. The sibling component `ExpiredValidateCodeModal` ("request one here" link) had the same problem and was fixed by resetting the root stack instead, with a comment explaining that navigate/goBack no-op from the public `/v/` route when it is the stack root:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/af37ee85da464d76cc6a95a0fa9c9414dc7f2b8c/src/components/ValidateCode/ExpiredValidateCodeModal.tsx#L46-L57

`ValidateCodeModal`'s `onLinkPress` override never got the same treatment.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

In `ValidateCodeModal`, replace the `onLinkPress` handler's `Navigation.goBack()` call with the codebase's established recovery pattern for the public `/v/` route: once navigation is ready, reset the root navigation state so its single route is `TAB_NAVIGATOR` (the same `navigationRef.reset` call, with the same explanatory comment, that `ExpiredValidateCodeModal` uses at the permalink above).

This lands the user on the correct "home page" in both auth states, because `TAB_NAVIGATOR` is registered in both root stacks — it hosts the public `SignInPage` when signed out and the Home screen when signed in:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/af37ee85da464d76cc6a95a0fa9c9414dc7f2b8c/src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/PublicScreens.tsx#L33-L37

We should also pass the same handler as `onBackButtonPress`, because the header back arrow that `FullPageNotFoundView` shows on narrow layouts defaults to the same dead `Navigation.goBack()` call and is unresponsive for the same reason.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

Removing the `onLinkPress` override so the view falls back to its default `Navigation.goBackToHome()`. That default routes through `goBack(ROUTES.HOME)`, which still depends on popping/rewriting an existing stack and is not the pattern this codebase uses for the stack-root `/v/` case, so the explicit reset is safer and consistent with the sibling components.

Alternatively, keep `Navigation.goBack()` when the navigator reports it can go back (the user reached `/v/` from inside the app) and only fall back to the stack reset otherwise. This preserves in-app back behavior, but the link's label promises "home page", so unconditionally going home is the more predictable behavior and matches the sibling components.

newProposal.body:
## Proposal

### What is the root cause of that problem?
The app's persistent product marketing overlay system (which manages bottom-right feature announcements) currently targets previous release items. To introduce the August 2026 update, new role-specific configurations and assets are required for workspace admins and regular users.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

1. **Announcement Configuration & Assets**:
   - Register a dedicated announcement identifier for August 2026 inside `ProductMarketingWindowUtils`.
   - Add image imports for both promo assets (`promo images.zip`) and wire them to their respective role variants.
   - For **Admin users**: set headline and body text via locale keys (`productMarketingWindow.roleTypes.admin`), with `getCtaRoute` returning the workspace vendors page if vendor rules are active or defaulting to workspace features.
   - For **Employee users**: set headline and body text via locale keys (`productMarketingWindow.roleTypes.member`), with `getCtaRoute` linking to `/settings/agents/new`.

2. **State Storage & Dismissal Logic**:
   - Tie dismissal state to the new August announcement key using the Onyx NVP engine (`NVP_LAST_DISMISSED_MARKETING_WINDOW`). Once a user clicks `Dismiss` or `Try it out`, the window will permanently hide for that key across sessions.

3. **Role Filtering**:
   - Utilize `ProductMarketingWindowManager` to evaluate admin rights for the current user's workspace, serving the Admin variant to admins and the Employee variant to all standard members.

4. **Localization & Quality Assurance**:
   - Include English translation strings in `src/languages/en.ts` and run locale updates.
   - Execute manual verification on Web, Desktop, iOS, and Android to confirm UI positioning, route navigation, and NVP persistence.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)
Creating an entirely new popup modal was considered, but leveraging the built-in `ProductMarketingWindow` framework provides native cross-platform support and seamless NVP dismissal tracking.

---
*Submitted by Snufkin*

This author already has two proposals in the conversation, one of them their own immediately preceding attempt, and the answer is still a different author’s proposal. A run that reports either of the same-author priors fails even though they are genuinely the most similar text present.

priorProposals.body:
## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.

The August 2026 product update needs a persistent bottom-right product marketing window, reusing the pattern built for the July update in issue #95791. There are two audience variants: admins should see "Enhanced vendor mapping" with a Try it out button that leads them to enable (or use) Vendors on their active admin workspace, and employees should see "Pre-built agents for you" with a Try it out button that opens the new-agent flow at `settings/agents/new`.

### What is the root cause of that problem?

This is a new feature request rather than a bug. The persistent window system built for #95791 is intentionally config-driven: exactly one announcement is active at a time, defined by `ACTIVE_PRODUCT_MARKETING_ANNOUNCEMENT` in `ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts`, and it currently still holds the July 2026 update (`productUpdateJuly2026`) with an admin-only variant:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1e9d3c3ef392d36aac215f5a93bc54f047211c59/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L52-L66

No August announcement has been authored yet, so nothing new is shown. Additionally, the announcement's CTA route builder currently only receives the target admin workspace ID, which is not enough for the August admin CTA — that CTA must branch on whether the workspace's Vendors feature is already enabled:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1e9d3c3ef392d36aac215f5a93bc54f047211c59/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L36-L37

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

Replace the active announcement in `ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts` with an August 2026 announcement using a new update key (for example `productUpdateAugust2026`). Because dismissal is tracked by comparing the update key against the `lastDismissedMarketingWindow` NVP, users who dismissed the July window will automatically see the August one — no changes to the dismissal, targeting, or visibility logic are needed:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1e9d3c3ef392d36aac215f5a93bc54f047211c59/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L68-L86

**Admin variant** — heading "Enhanced vendor mapping", body "Create vendors and custom rules for easy mapping to major accounting packages.", CTA "Try it out". The CTA should navigate to the Vendors page (`workspaces/<policyID>/vendors`, the existing `WORKSPACE_VENDORS` route) when the target workspace's Vendors feature is already on, and otherwise to the More features page (`workspaces/<policyID>/more-features`, the existing `WORKSPACE_MORE_FEATURES` route) where the admin can turn Vendors on. Whether Vendors is on is exactly what the existing `hasVendorFeature` helper answers (vendor-matching beta plus a supported accounting connection), the same check the More features page uses for its Vendors toggle:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1e9d3c3ef392d36aac215f5a93bc54f047211c59/src/libs/PolicyUtils.ts#L2438-L2443

To support that branch, extend the announcement variant's CTA route builder so it receives the resolved target admin workspace's full policy object and the vendor-matching beta state, not just the workspace ID. `ProductMarketingWindowManager` already holds the full active admin policy objects (it currently narrows them down to `targetAdminPolicyID`), and it can read the beta via the existing permissions hook, so it passes both into the route builder:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1e9d3c3ef392d36aac215f5a93bc54f047211c59/src/components/ProductMarketingWindow/ProductMarketingWindowManager.tsx#L67-L68

The existing target-workspace selection already implements "their active workspace they are an admin on" (the active policy when the user is an admin on it, otherwise their first active admin workspace), so it is kept as is.

**Member (employee) variant** — heading "Pre-built agents for you", body "Use pre-built or custom agents to code, split, and submit expenses automatically on your behalf.", CTA "Try it out" navigating to the existing `SETTINGS_AGENTS_NEW` route (`settings/agents/new`), which matches the URL requested in the issue. The member variant is already optional in the announcement type and the manager already falls back to it for users with no active admin workspace, so adding it is pure configuration:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1e9d3c3ef392d36aac215f5a93bc54f047211c59/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L40-L50

**Copy and translations** — add the August heading/body/CTA strings for both variants under the existing `productMarketingWindow` namespace in `en.ts`, remove the now-unused July keys, and generate the other locales the standard way.

**Visuals** — the window's visual field already accepts either a bundled marketing image or an existing app illustration. Once the design mocks land (vendor-list image for the admin case, agents-list image for the employee case), add them as bundled assets the same way the July promo image was added; until then an existing relevant illustration can serve as the interim visual so the window is fully functional for review.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

Building the August window as a second, parallel announcement alongside the July one was ruled out — the system is deliberately single-active with no stacking or queueing, and replacing the active announcement is the intended release mechanism. Always sending the admin CTA to the More features page (skipping the vendors-enabled branch) was also ruled out because the issue explicitly asks for the direct destination when Vendors is already on.

priorProposals.body:
## Proposal

### What is the root cause of that problem?

The persistent bottom-right product marketing window system already exists (built in #95791 and driven by the dismissed-product-training NVP, e.g. the `DismissedProductTraining` selector pattern used for other banners):

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/pages/workspace/rules/PolicyRulesPageRevamp.tsx#L75-L79

There is simply no window definition for the August update, so neither the admin "Enhanced vendor mapping" card nor the employee "Pre-built agents" card renders, and their two "Try it out" destinations are not wired.

The admin CTA is also non-trivial because its target depends on whether the admin's workspace can even reach Vendors. Vendors lives inside Rules, and Rules access for a workspace is gated by `canPolicyAccessFeature` (Collect needs the Rules revamp beta, otherwise Control only):

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/libs/PolicyUtils.ts#L1453-L1465

and the Vendors toggle itself is only exposed when `VENDOR_MATCHING` is enabled on the More features page:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/pages/workspace/WorkspaceMoreFeaturesPage/index.tsx#L61-L95

So a blind link to a fixed `{policyID}/more-features` would break for members who are not admins of that workspace or whose plan cannot access Rules.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

1. Register two new product-update window entries in the same persistent-window config used by #95791 (title/subtext/image/buttons per the deliverables), each dismissible via the existing `dismissProductTraining` flow used by `RulesGeneralTab`:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/pages/workspace/rules/tabs/RulesGeneralTab.tsx#L23-L49

2. Admin case "Try it out": resolve the workspace where the current user is an admin, then route through the existing More features route. Reuse `WORKSPACE_MORE_FEATURES.getRoute(policyID)` already used on that page:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/pages/workspace/WorkspaceMoreFeaturesPage/index.tsx#L353-L387

When Vendors is already on for that workspace, deep-link straight to the Rules Vendors screen instead of More features:

```ts
const canAccessRules = canPolicyAccessFeature(policy, CONST.POLICY.MORE_FEATURES.ARE_RULES_ENABLED, isRulesRevampEnabled);
const vendorsAlreadyOn = isVendorMatchingEnabled && canAccessRules && arePolicyRulesEnabled(policy, policyCategories, isRulesRevampEnabled);
Navigation.navigate(vendorsAlreadyOn ? ROUTES.WORKSPACE_RULES.getRoute(policyID) : ROUTES.WORKSPACE_MORE_FEATURES.getRoute(policyID));
```

This mirrors the exact enablement checks in `useControlOnlyRuleUpgradeRedirect`, so the CTA never lands a member on a page their plan cannot use:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/hooks/useControlOnlyRuleUpgradeRedirect.ts#L25-L45

3. Employee case "Try it out": navigate to the new-agent route (`/settings/agents/new`) using its `ROUTES` constant, matching the CTA behavior of the existing `AgentPromotionalBanner` in `RulesGeneralTab`.

This adds the missing window definitions and gives each CTA a destination that respects admin membership and Rules/Vendors availability.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

Always link the admin CTA to a fixed `more-features` URL and let `AccessOrNotFoundWrapper` redirect, but that flashes an inaccessible page for non-admins or non-Rules plans, so resolving the correct workspace and gate up front is cleaner.

**Reminder:** Please use plain English, be brief and avoid jargon. Feel free to use images, charts or pseudo-code if necessary. Do not post large multi-line diffs or write walls of text. Do not create PRs unless you have been hired for this job.

priorProposals.author: sniff
priorProposals.body:
## Proposal

### What is the root cause of that problem?

This is new-content work, not a code defect. The persistent bottom-right window built in #95791 is content-driven: it renders whatever `ACTIVE_PRODUCT_MARKETING_ANNOUNCEMENT` contains, and that constant is still pinned to the July 2026 announcement (admin-only, no member variant):

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L57-L66

One gap does need a small code change: the August admin CTA must branch on whether Vendors is already enabled ("more features" page vs. the direct vendors URL), but the current `getCtaRoute` contract only receives the target workspace ID, so a variant can't inspect the policy's feature state:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L36-L37

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

1. In `ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts`, replace the July announcement with a new one using a fresh `updateKey` (e.g. `productUpdateAugust2026`) so users who dismissed July see August. Fill both variants: `admin` = "Enhanced vendor mapping" with the vendor-list marketing image, `member` = "Pre-built agents for you" with the agents-list image, both with a "Try it out" CTA. New strings go under `productMarketingWindow` in `en.ts`/`es.ts` next to the existing July block:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/languages/en.ts#L10534-L10540

2. Widen `getCtaRoute` to receive the target admin `Policy` object (and the vendor-matching beta flag) instead of just the ID. The manager already resolves the full policy list, so it can pass the found policy through where it currently passes only `targetAdminPolicyID`:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/components/ProductMarketingWindow/ProductMarketingWindowManager.tsx#L67-L68

The admin variant's `getCtaRoute` then reuses the same check the More Features page uses, `hasVendorFeature`:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7ad89cbb22a57807dfa808876b39337164f5b281/src/libs/PolicyUtils.ts#L2438-L2442

returning `ROUTES.WORKSPACE_VENDORS.getRoute(policy.id)` when vendors are on, otherwise `ROUTES.WORKSPACE_MORE_FEATURES.getRoute(policy.id)`. The member variant's `getCtaRoute` simply returns `ROUTES.SETTINGS_AGENTS_NEW.getRoute()`. All display/dismiss/precedence logic in the manager and window component stays untouched.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

Keep `getCtaRoute(policyID)` as-is and do the vendors-enabled branch inside the manager's `completeCta`. Rejected because it leaks announcement-specific logic into the shared manager; keeping routing decisions inside the variant keeps future updates content-only.

priorProposals.author: too-ticky
priorProposals.body:
## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.

Ship the August 2026 product update persistent bottom-right window: an admin variant ("Enhanced vendor mapping") with a CTA that deep-links into that workspace's **vendors page** when Vendors is already on, or falls back to **more-features** otherwise; and an employee variant ("Pre-built agents for you") whose CTA opens `settings/agents/new` — but only for accounts that can actually reach that route.

### What is the root cause of that problem?

No August announcement exists in the config-driven system. Authoring it looks mechanical until you hit three non-obvious landmines.

**Landmine 1: `areVendorsEnabled` does not exist as a Policy field.** A grep of `src/` returns zero hits on any property named `areVendorsEnabled` or `vendorsEnabled`. Vendors enablement is a *derived* predicate:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/6ed77eddc647cb35737bdffa0f19ccce6dabf468/src/libs/PolicyUtils.ts#L2445-L2450

`hasVendorFeature` reads `policy.connections` to check whether the relevant accounting connection has `vendorMatching` active. This matters because the manager currently discards the policy object and exposes only `policy.id`:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/6ed77eddc647cb35737bdffa0f19ccce6dabf468/src/components/ProductMarketingWindow/ProductMarketingWindowManager.tsx#L66-L68

Calling `hasVendorFeature(policyID)` is a type error — calling it with only an ID and expecting a connections-derived answer returns wrong results.

**Landmine 2: Connections are only hydrated for the currently-active workspace.** `usePolicyConnectionsPrefetch` fetches connections at startup for the single active policy:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/6ed77eddc647cb35737bdffa0f19ccce6dabf468/src/hooks/usePolicyConnectionsPrefetch.ts#L22-L31

The announcement targets the *first admin workspace* when the user's active workspace is not one they admin. For that fallback workspace, `policy.connections` may be empty at render time, so `hasVendorFeature` returns `false` and every admin gets routed to more-features regardless. This is acceptable (more-features is the issue's specified default and itself prefetches connections before rendering the Vendors row), but the reasoning must be explicit — otherwise a future reviewer "fixes" the fallback with a gratuitous `openPolicyAccountingPage` call that races the prefetch.

**Landmine 3: The employee CTA dead-ends for custom-agent accounts.** `settings/agents/new` is wrapped in `withAgentAccessDenied`, which silently redirects `isCustomAgent` users to Profile:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/6ed77eddc647cb35737bdffa0f19ccce6dabf468/src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/withAgentAccessDenied.tsx#L60-L72

Custom-agent users would see the "Pre-built agents for you" card, tap the CTA, and land on their own Profile with no explanation. The window must be suppressed entirely for agent accounts, not just the CTA.

Additionally, the `VENDOR_MATCHING` beta gates Vendors visibility on more-features:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/6ed77eddc647cb35737bdffa0f19ccce6dabf468/src/pages/workspace/WorkspaceMoreFeaturesPage/index.tsx#L461-L466

An admin outside the beta who lands on more-features would see no Vendors row. That admin should fall through to the employee variant rather than receive a broken admin experience.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

**`src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts`** — widen the CTA callback's input from a bare policy ID to a context object that carries the resolved `Policy` (for `hasVendorFeature`) and a beta-check function (for routing decisions):

```ts
type ProductMarketingAnnouncementCtaContext = {
    adminPolicy?: Policy;
    isBetaEnabled: (beta: Beta) => boolean;
};
```

Register the August announcement and add the two promo images from the attached zip to `assets/images/`:

```ts
const ACTIVE_PRODUCT_MARKETING_ANNOUNCEMENT: ProductMarketingAnnouncement | null = {
    updateKey: 'productUpdateAugust2026',
    admin: {
        visual: {type: 'image', source: August26VendorsPromoImage},
        heading: 'productMarketingWindow.vendorMapping.heading',
        body:    'productMarketingWindow.vendorMapping.body',
        ctaLabel:'productMarketingWindow.vendorMapping.cta',
        getCtaRoute: ({adminPolicy, isBetaEnabled}) =>
            hasVendorFeature(adminPolicy, isBetaEnabled(CONST.BETAS.VENDOR_MATCHING))
                ? ROUTES.WORKSPACE_VENDORS.getRoute(adminPolicy?.id)
                : ROUTES.WORKSPACE_MORE_FEATURES.getRoute(adminPolicy?.id),
    },
    member: {
        visual: {type: 'image', source: August26AgentsPromoImage},
        heading: 'productMarketingWindow.agents.heading',
```

## Proposal

### What is the root cause of that problem?

New Feature.

The persistent bottom-right window built in #95791 is deliberately **single-active**: exactly one announcement is defined by `ACTIVE_PRODUCT_MARKETING_ANNOUNCEMENT` in `ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts`, dismissal is keyed on its `updateKey` (compared against the `NVP_LAST_DISMISSED_MARKETING_WINDOW` NVP), and it currently still holds the **July** update with an admin-only variant — so nothing new renders:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1df21965ec26cee4e5d2dc0e1e2a6b1483a2cdb2/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L57-L66

The one structural gap for August is the admin CTA. The variant's route builder only receives the workspace ID — [`ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L36-L37`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1df21965ec26cee4e5d2dc0e1e2a6b1483a2cdb2/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L36-L37) — which is not enough to branch on whether Vendors is already on for that workspace, as the "if Vendors is turned on, take them to the direct URL" deliverable requires.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

**Replace the active announcement** in `ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts` with an August one under a new key (e.g. `productUpdateAugust2026`). Because dismissal compares `updateKey` against the NVP, users who dismissed July automatically see August — the visibility, targeting, and dismissal logic at [`ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L84-L86`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1df21965ec26cee4e5d2dc0e1e2a6b1483a2cdb2/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L84-L86) is unchanged.

**Widen `getCtaRoute` to one context object** — `(ctx: {policyID?: string; policy?: OnyxEntry<Policy>; isVendorMatchingBetaEnabled?: boolean}) => Route`. The member variant just ignores the fields it doesn't need, so a single shape covers both. This builder has exactly one caller and one definition site (below), so the signature change touches only those two places.

**Admin variant** — heading `Enhanced vendor mapping`, body `Create vendors and custom rules for easy mapping to major accounting packages.`, CTA `Try it out`. Its `getCtaRoute` returns `WORKSPACE_VENDORS.getRoute(policyID)` when Vendors is on, else `WORKSPACE_MORE_FEATURES.getRoute(policyID)`. "Vendors is on" is exactly `hasVendorFeature(policy, isVendorMatchingBetaEnabled)` (vendor-matching beta + a supported accounting connection) — the same predicate the More features page uses for its Vendors toggle, so the CTA and the toggle agree:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1df21965ec26cee4e5d2dc0e1e2a6b1483a2cdb2/src/libs/PolicyUtils.ts#L2445-L2450

[`WorkspaceMoreFeaturesPage/index.tsx#L461-L466`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1df21965ec26cee4e5d2dc0e1e2a6b1483a2cdb2/src/pages/workspace/WorkspaceMoreFeaturesPage/index.tsx#L461-L466)

**In `ProductMarketingWindowManager`**, pass that context. It already holds the full active-admin policy objects (it currently narrows them to the ID at [`#L67-L68`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1df21965ec26cee4e5d2dc0e1e2a6b1483a2cdb2/src/components/ProductMarketingWindow/ProductMarketingWindowManager.tsx#L67-L68)) and can read the beta with `usePermissions().isBetaEnabled(CONST.BETAS.VENDOR_MATCHING)`, so the CTA call becomes `variant.getCtaRoute({policyID: targetAdminPolicyID, policy: targetAdminPolicy, isVendorMatchingBetaEnabled})`:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1df21965ec26cee4e5d2dc0e1e2a6b1483a2cdb2/src/components/ProductMarketingWindow/ProductMarketingWindowManager.tsx#L87

**Member (employee) variant** — heading `Pre-built agents for you`, body `Use pre-built or custom agents to code, split, and submit expenses automatically on your behalf.`, CTA `Try it out`, `getCtaRoute` returning `SETTINGS_AGENTS_NEW.getRoute()` (its object-arg signature yields `settings/agents/new` with no `policyID`), matching the requested URL. The variant is already optional in the type and the manager already falls back to it for users with no active admin workspace, so this is pure config.

**Copy** — under the existing `productMarketingWindow.roleTypes` namespace, update `admin.heading`/`admin.body` and add a `member` sub-object; `cta` stays `Try it out` (no new CTA string), then generate `es` + all locales:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1df21965ec26cee4e5d2dc0e1e2a6b1483a2cdb2/src/languages/en.ts#L10498-L10506

**Visuals** — add the two bundled promo images from the attached `promo images.zip` the same way `July26PromoImage` is imported at the top of the utils file, one per variant.

**Caveat worth stating:** `hasVendorFeature` reads `policy.connections`, which this window (unlike the More features page's `usePolicyConnectionsPrefetch`) never prefetches. If the target workspace's connections aren't in Onyx yet, it returns `false` and the admin CTA routes to **more-features** — which is precisely the spec's default destination, so the fallback is safe rather than wrong.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

- **The `dismissProductTraining` / product-training NVP approach** (register two window entries, gate the admin link on `canPolicyAccessFeature` + the Rules-revamp beta) — this is the wrong subsystem: the persistent window is the single-active `ACTIVE_PRODUCT_MARKETING_ANNOUNCEMENT`, dismissed via `NVP_LAST_DISMISSED_MARKETING_WINDOW`, which does not stack or queue; and "Vendors on" is `hasVendorFeature`, not Rules access.
- **Extending `getCtaRoute` with extra positional args** (policy + beta alongside the ID) works, but a single context object keeps the member variant — which needs none of them — from carrying unused parameters, and leaves room for future variants.
- **A second, parallel announcement alongside July** — ruled out; the system is single-active by design, and replacing the active announcement is the intended release mechanism.

# Proposal

## Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.
We need to author the content for the **August 2026 product update** in the existing "persistent bottom-right product marketing window" (first built for issue #95791), with two audience-targeted variants:
- **Admin variant** — "Enhanced vendor mapping": title, subtext, a vendor/accounting-packages image, and a "Try it out" CTA that opens the admin's active workspace's More Features page (`workspaces/:policyID/more-features`) — unless the Vendors feature is already turned on for that workspace, in which case it should go straight to the Vendors page.
- **Employee variant** — "Pre-built agents for you": title, subtext, an agents-list image, and a "Try it out" CTA that opens `new.expensify.com/settings/agents/new`.

## What is the root cause of that problem?
This isn't a bug — it's a content/config change to a feature that already exists and is architected exactly for this: swap in a new announcement. Nothing needs to be built from scratch; we need to (a) replace the single active announcement's content/CTA data, and (b) extend the CTA-resolution logic just enough to support the admin variant's conditional destination.

**Where the current (July 2026) announcement lives — this is the single source of truth for content, per-audience variants, and CTA routing:**
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c926b197/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L57-L66

Today `ACTIVE_PRODUCT_MARKETING_ANNOUNCEMENT` only defines an `admin` variant (no `member` variant), and `admin.getCtaRoute` is a simple one-line route builder that ignores any feature state — it just forwards the admin policy ID into `ROUTES.WORKSPACE_MEMBERS.getRoute`. The type only allows `getCtaRoute` to receive an `adminPolicyID`:
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c926b197/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L23-L38

That's the gap: our new admin CTA must branch ("Vendors already on?" → Vendors page, else → More Features page), but there's currently no way to pass that "is the feature already on" signal into `getCtaRoute`.

**Where the variant is resolved and the CTA is actually invoked** — this is where the target admin policy is already computed, and where the extra "is Vendors on" signal needs to be assembled and threaded through:
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c926b197/src/components/ProductMarketingWindow/ProductMarketingWindowManager.tsx#L47-L98
Specifically, `targetAdminPolicyID` (line 67) is derived from the full policy objects already fetched via `activeAdminPolicies` (line 49-51), and `completeCta` (lines 84-88) is what calls `variant.getCtaRoute(targetAdminPolicyID)` before navigating.

**The "is Vendors on" check already exists and is exactly the right function to reuse** — it's the same predicate that drives the (currently locked) Vendors toggle on the More Features page, checking whether a supported accounting integration (QBO/Intacct/Xero) is connected in vendor-matching mode, gated behind the `vendorMatching` beta:
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c926b197/src/libs/PolicyUtils.ts#L2445-L2450
It's consumed the same way in `WorkspaceMoreFeaturesPage`:
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c926b197/src/pages/workspace/WorkspaceMoreFeaturesPage/index.tsx#L461-L479

For the employee variant's destination, `settings/agents/new` already exists as `ROUTES.SETTINGS_AGENTS_NEW`:
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c926b197/src/ROUTES.ts#L2003-L2012

One more relevant fact: the "custom agents" feature is still beta-gated elsewhere in the app (e.g. the AI features promo modal only shows its "Build your own agents" page when `CONST.BETAS.CUSTOM_AGENT` is enabled for the account):
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c926b197/src/components/AIFeaturesPromoModal.tsx#L26-L27
`NewAgentPage` itself (behind `SETTINGS_AGENTS_NEW`) does not re-check that beta, so a non-beta employee who clicks "Try it out" would land on a page that isn't really meant for them yet — the marketing window should not advertise this to accounts without the beta, mirroring how the rest of the app treats this feature as opt-in.

## What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

**1. Add the new images as static assets**, analogous to the existing `assets/images/july26-promo.png` import at the top of `ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts` (line 1) — one for the vendor-mapping admin visual, one for the pre-built-agents employee visual (sourced from the "promo images.zip" attached to this issue).

**2. Replace `ACTIVE_PRODUCT_MARKETING_ANNOUNCEMENT`** in
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c926b197/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L57-L66
with a new entry using a fresh `updateKey` (e.g. `'productUpdateAugust2026'` — must be new so it isn't treated as already-dismissed by users who dismissed July's window), defining both `admin` and `member` variants with the copy from the issue, and CTA routes:

```ts
admin: {
    visual: {type: 'image', source: Aug26VendorMappingPromoImage},
    heading: 'productMarketingWindow.roleTypes.admin.heading',
    body: 'productMarketingWindow.roleTypes.admin.body',
    ctaLabel: 'productMarketingWindow.roleTypes.admin.cta',
    getCtaRoute: (adminPolicyID, isVendorFeatureActive) =>
        isVendorFeatureActive ? ROUTES.WORKSPACE_VENDORS.getRoute(adminPolicyID) : ROUTES.WORKSPACE_MORE_FEATURES.getRoute(adminPolicyID),
},
member: {
    visual: {type: 'image', source: Aug26AgentsPromoImage},
    heading: 'productMarketingWindow.roleTypes.member.heading',
    body: 'productMarketingWindow.roleTypes.member.body',
    ctaLabel: 'productMarketingWindow.roleTypes.member.cta',
    getCtaRoute: () => ROUTES.SETTINGS_AGENTS_NEW.getRoute(),
},
```

**3. Widen the `getCtaRoute` signature by one optional param** in the same file so the admin variant can branch on feature state:
```ts
getCtaRoute: (adminPolicyID?: string, isVendorFeatureActive?: boolean) => Route;
```
This is additive and backward-compatible — existing test doubles in `tests/unit/ProductMarketingWindowUtilsTest.ts` and `tests/unit/ProductMarketingWindowTest.tsx` define `getCtaRoute` with zero or one argument, which remains a valid implementation of the widened function type (TypeScript allows an implementation to ignore trailing params).

**4. In `ProductMarketingWindowManager.tsx`**, compute the two new pieces of eligibility state alongside the existing `usePermissions`-style hooks and pass them through:
- Resolve the full target admin `Policy` object (the manager already finds it via `activeAdminPolicies.find(...)` at line 67 to get the ID — reuse the same lookup to keep the object, not just the ID).
- Add `const {isBetaEnabled} = usePermissions();` and compute `isVendorFeatureActive = hasVendorFeature(targetAdminPolicy, isBetaEnabled(CONST.BETAS.VENDOR_MATCHING))`, importing `hasVendorFeature` from `@user/PolicyUtils`.
- Pass it into the CTA call: `Navigation.navigate(variant.getCtaRoute(targetAdminPolicyID, isVendorFeatureActive))` (line 87).
- Gate the employee/member variant on `isBetaEnabled(CONST.BETAS.CUSTOM_AGENT)`: when the resolved audience is "member" (not admin) and this beta is disabled, treat the announcement as having no eligible variant for that user (hide the window), the same way `getProductMarketingAnnouncementVariant` already hides the window when there's no `member` variant defined at all. Concretely, this means passing an extra `isMemberVariantEligible` boolean into `getProductMarketingAnnouncementVariant` in `ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts` (https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c926b197/src/libs/ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts#L77-L86) and returning `undefined` instead of `announcement.member` when it's false.

**5. Add the translation keys** under `productMarketingWindow.roleTypes` in `src/languages/en.ts` (and other locale files), following the existing shape at
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c926b197/src/languages/en.ts#L10498-L10506
adding a sibling `member` (or `employee`) key next to `admin`, each with `heading`, `body`, and `cta` using the exact copy given in the issue.

### Edge cases handled
- **Vendors beta/integration not enabled for the target workspace**: `hasVendorFeature` already returns `false` unless the `vendorMatching` beta is on *and* a supported integration is connected in vendor-matching mode, so the CTA correctly falls back to the More Features page instead of a Vendors page the admin can't act on.
- **Non-beta employees**: gating the member variant on `CONST.BETAS.CUSTOM_AGENT` prevents advertising agents to accounts where the feature isn't available yet, consistent with how `AIFeaturesPromoModal` already treats this beta.
- **Loading state**: `ProductMarketingWindowManager` already blocks rendering until `activeAdminPoliciesMetadata` (and friends) finish loading before computing `targetAdminPolicyID`/variant, so the new `hasVendorFeature` check (which depends on `policy.connections`, part of the same policy object) isn't evaluated against stale/partial data.
- **Offline**: no new network calls are introduced; `hasVendorFeature` and `isBetaEnabled` are both pure/local reads of already-synced Onyx data, same as the existing admin-vs-member resolution.
- **Web/iOS/Android**: no new platform-specific code paths — the window's rendering, portal, and styling are unchanged; only the content and CTA-route data change.
- **Existing callers**: `getCtaRoute`'s widened signature doesn't break the July-2026 admin variant's shape (it's being replaced wholesale) nor the unit/UI test mocks, since the added parameter is optional and appended at the end.
- **Dismissal**: using a brand-new `updateKey` ensures users who already dismissed the July 2026 window still see the new August window (per the existing single-slot, no-fallthrough dismissal design already documented at lines 52-56 of `ProductMarketingWindowUtils.ts`).

## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.

On the Spend (Search) page the date filter and the date column are both just labelled "Date", which is ambiguous next to Submitted/Approved/Posted/Exported. The filter option should read **"Created date"** and the column header **"Created"**, for every search Type.

### What is the root cause of that problem?

There is no Search-scoped label for this field. Both places render the generic key `common.date`, and they read it through **three independent sources**, so no single edit can produce the two different strings the issue asks for.

1. The string is `common.date: 'Date'` — [en.ts#L168](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/languages/en.ts#L168). It has 23 references in 16 files (expense edit, personal details, travel, wallet, `MoneyRequestView`), so its value is not ours to change.
2. **Source A — filter label:** `FILTER_VIEW_MAP[SYNTAX_FILTER_KEYS.DATE].labelKey = 'common.date'` — [SearchUIUtils.ts#L5527-L5530](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L5527-L5530).
3. **Source B — column label:** `getSearchColumnTranslationKey()` maps `TABLE_COLUMNS.DATE` → `'common.date'` — [SearchUIUtils.ts#L4508-L4513](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L4508-L4513).
4. **Source C — the header rows do not use B.** `SearchTableHeader` hardcodes `translationKey: 'common.date'` a third time, once per data type, rendered by [SortableTableHeader.tsx#L92](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/components/Search/SortableTableHeader.tsx#L92).

Structural cause: **one overloaded generic key is doing three jobs** — generic "Date", the Search filter label, the Search column label — and the issue requires those to diverge.

Every affected path:

*Source A → "Created date":*
- Filters list row — [FilterList.tsx#L54](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/components/Search/FilterComponents/AdvancedFilters/FilterList.tsx#L54)
- Filter page title — [SearchAdvancedFiltersContentBase.tsx#L61](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/pages/Search/SearchAdvancedFiltersContentPage/SearchAdvancedFiltersContentBase.tsx#L61)

*Sources B + C → "Created":*
- Expense headers — [SearchTableHeader.tsx#L44-L48](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx#L44-L48); Task — [#L209-L212](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx#L209-L212); Expense-report — [#L252-L255](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e13e30c175c1a984ad4faa11615929ea25360566/src/components/Search/SearchTableHeader.tsx#L252-L255)
